chapters.title: Chapter 51
paragraphs: Swish, swish, swish!
Swords, axes, maces.
Dozens of weapons poured down like rain. But I could see every one of them clearly—where each attack was headed and how.
I slipped through the gaps.
Slice—
It started with me taking the head off a C-rank monster, a Lizardman Warrior. As the spearhead swept through a semicircle, blood spurted in every direction.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System You defeated Lv. 40 Lizardman Warrior! - You defeated Lv. 41 Swamp Lizardman! - You defeated Lv. 40 Swamp Lizardman...
Keeee...
The survivors hesitated and backed away. The same creatures that had been pouring out killing intent at the enemy of their kin were now trembling with fear.
But that lasted only a moment.
Gwoooaar!
System Boss Monster Lv. 52 Lizardman Great Chieftain has appeared! - The Skill Battle Cry is being used!

It was at least twice the size of the others, with a gigantic mace in its hand. The Lizardman Chieftain’s roar exploded through the air. At the appearance of their leader, the retreating Lizardmen came to their senses and formed ranks.
I was wondering why this was wrapping up so easily.
Team Leader Choi’s unhurried voice came from behind me.
“Can you handle it?”
“Is that something someone who hasn’t lifted a finger for days should be asking?”
“This is different. It’s a C-rank Gate.”
“Then help, why don’t you.”
Team Leader Choi thought it over before answering.
“I don’t think I can. I’m wearing a limited edition today. It’d break my heart if blood splattered on it.”
“...Should I make it hurt for real?”
The longer we talked, the more my gut burned and the back of my head throbbed, as if I were suffering an Internal Injury. I’d rather fight the monsters.
As I took a long stride forward, Team Leader Choi tossed out a single line.
“Retreat is another option.”
The man standing behind me with his arms folded so blood wouldn’t splatter on his limited-edition Equipment had made a pretty good point.
The kind that made me want to hit him.
And then...
“Why bother when there’s a better way?”
Ahead of us, the monsters surged forward like a wave, led by the Lizardman Great Chieftain. C- and D-rank monsters mixed together—a force an ordinary C-rank Hunter wouldn’t even dream of facing.
An ordinary C-rank Hunter, that is.
Status Window, open.
Ding.
The System answered at once.
A week had passed since I’d started working as a Hunter again. On the Status Window, the number 40 and the line at the very bottom shone brightly.
System Remaining Points: 100
Since returning to reality, I hadn’t spent a single Remaining Point. Purely out of curiosity.
How far can I go as I am now?
But hoarding them any longer would be reckless.
Assign 30 each to Strength and Stamina. Assign 40 to Agility.
The next moment, my Remaining Points hit zero.
In exchange, new power surged from deep inside me. I was no longer the same Jin Taekyung I’d been only seconds ago.
Yeah. This is it.
I was still trembling with exhilaration when—
Gwaaaar!
The Lizardman Great Chieftain charged with a roar. I thrust my spear toward the gigantic mace casting a shadow over me.
“One Annihilation.”
At the tip of my spear, a path through the wind opened.
“Hah.”
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—let out a hollow laugh.
A dense fog of blood hung over the wetlands, and beneath it lay the sprawled corpses of the monsters.
What the hell...
Dozens of monsters, including the boss, had been slaughtered in an instant. All of it by the spear of a C-rank Hunter who had reawakened only a few days ago.
Is something like this even possible?
It was a question he had carried since the day he first met Jin Taekyung.
That day, they had gone to an E-rank Gate without much thought. There, Taekyung had overwhelmingly overpowered a Rare Monster that normally took a couple of C-rank Hunters to bring down.
And on top of that, the strength he had shown over the past few days was...
Calling him a C-rank Hunter is a joke.
The reason Choi had begun raiding alone with Taekyung was simple.
He wanted to see how far this fascinating man could go.
And he wanted to keep anyone else from finding out.
But then a thought occurred to him.
Could he be stronger than me...?
No. No.
That was impossible.
Choi Minwoo forced the thought aside. Then Jin Taekyung caught his eye.
He was clutching the boss monster’s corpse—its upper body completely gone—and wailing in grief.
“No! My hide! This was expensive!”
...There was no way a man like that could be.
No. He mustn’t be.
Choi Minwoo suddenly felt cheated.
Burning Friday. Bulgeum, for short.
Other people in their twenties would be drinking in groups and drifting in and out of clubs. I spent it running Gates with Team Leader Choi.
Once in the morning. Twice in the afternoon.
By the time we finished three C-rank Gates and came back out, night had already fallen.
“Thank you for your hard work, Young Master.”
The face was familiar now. Team Leader Choi addressed the rugged-looking man in his forties like this:
“Thank you for your hard work too, Butler Kim.”
Butler Kim. Not a secretary—a butler.
The word was so detached from reality that I thought I’d misheard it at first.
I’ve only ever met church deacons.
Back when I was a snot-nosed kid getting a thousand won a week in allowance, one of them had been the bastard who forced me to hand over a hundred won as a tithe.
Of course, he hadn’t called me Young Master. When I dug in and refused to pay, he’d even muttered that I was the child of Satan.
And at seven years old, I was the kind of kid who always asked when something made me curious.
“Mom. Are you Satan?”
“Huh? Satan?”
“Yeah. The church deacon said I was Satan’s child. I’m your kid, so that makes you Satan, right? Right?”
Those words turned my mother into Satan.
I never got to eat the church tteokbokki again, and the church deacon nearly went to be with the Lord.
Thinking back on it, my life really had been one hell of a variety show.
“Did you have something to say...?”
Butler Kim’s voice pulled me back.
“Nothing. I was just thinking about something else.”
“Let’s call it a day.”
Team Leader Choi had already changed into street clothes. In a lightweight tailored suit, he looked just like a celebrity.
Life is so damn unfair.
I grumbled inwardly as I started taking off my Equipment. Carefully, of course. I’d looked up the price on the first day, and it was...
Never mind. Let’s not go there.
While Butler Kim loaded the Equipment into the car, I asked Team Leader Choi, “What time should I come in tomorrow?”
“Tomorrow?”
Team Leader Choi sounded puzzled.
“Today is Friday.”
“Yes.”
“And tomorrow is Saturday.”
“I know Saturday comes after Friday.”
Does he take me for a fucking idiot?
“No, I mean...”
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.
“Don’t tell me you’re planning to work this weekend too.”
“...Isn’t that obvious?”
Team Leader Choi asked with a shocked look,
“If you don’t take weekends off, when do you rest?”
“Um. When I can’t find work?”
“How often is that?”
“I don’t know. If I get a lot of time off, maybe once a month?”
“You used to belong to a Guild. You worked weekends then too?”
“I did if there was work.”
“Isn’t that a violation of the Hunter Labor Law?”
Even Team Leader Choi, who seemed perfect, didn’t know one thing.
How the world actually worked.
I let out a short laugh.
“What small or midsize Guild follows that to the letter? They all throw in extra pay and send you out on raids. Worked out for me, anyway.”
“Excuse me? You liked it?”
“I go to the day-labor agency on weekends. Getting extra pay from the Guild beats going there. They paid us cash on the spot to keep it off the books.”
“That’s just how it is.”
Team Leader Choi shook his head in disbelief.
“Our Guild follows the Labor Law. Provisional contracts are no exception.”
That’s a shame. Looks like I’ll have to go to the day-labor agency this weekend.
As I smacked my lips over the missed opportunity, Team Leader Choi gave me that peculiar look of his.
“Why do you push yourself so hard?”
“Why?”
“You’re a C-rank Hunter now. You can afford to take it a little easier.”
“That’s...”
Because I don’t know when the System might disappear.
I caught the words before they burst out of my throat. That was my secret—something I couldn’t tell anyone.
“No particular reason. You have to row while the tide is in.”
“If you keep working like that, you’ll break the oars. Think about the people in the boat with you.”
“The people in the boat with me? You, Team Leader?”
“Well, for example...”
Team Leader Choi paused before continuing.
“Your family, perhaps.”
Family.

It was only one word, but warmth seeped into every corner of my body. We talked on the phone now and then, but I hadn’t seen them in more than two months. Counting the time I’d spent in Murim, it had been three.
Has it already been that long?
Ever since my father died, my life had felt like a car driving uphill.
So I’d had no choice but to keep my foot on the gas. It felt as though I’d roll backward the moment I let up. As though the engine might die at any second.
“Anyway, weekends are off. Don’t even think about going to the day-labor agency. Rest. That would be a contract violation.”
“Oh. Okay.”
Forcing me to rest this hard... Maybe this guy Choi isn’t such a bad person after all...
No.
I couldn’t let myself get taken in by a little emotional appeal. Not after all the hell I’d gone through on my own.
Team Leader Choi is an exploitative employer. An exploitative employer.

It was obvious he only wanted me resting on the weekend so he could work me to the bone starting next week. It was the mentality of a slave plantation owner who didn’t want his worker wasting stamina somewhere else.
What a vicious man.
“Everything is ready, Young Master.”
Butler Kim had returned after loading the Equipment.
That man’s suffering under an exploitative employer too. It’s almost ten at night, and he still hasn’t gotten off work.
“Ah. What about the thing I mentioned?”
“I brought it.”
“Give it to him.”
At the exploitative employer’s command, Butler Kim held out the small box in his hands.
“Please take this, Hunter.”
To me.
“Huh? Me?”
It looked like a box of tonic drinks. I blinked at it until a thought flashed through my mind.
I asked carefully, “Don’t tell me this is money.”
“We contracted for weekly pay. Did you forget?”
I had. I’d assumed I would get it on Sunday.
I took the box, still dazed. It was heavy.
“Do you normally pay in cash?”
“Of course not.”
“Then...”
“You said you preferred cash, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Especially crisp new bills.”
I’d mentioned it in passing yesterday—or the day before. I hadn’t expected it to come back like this.
My opinion of the exploitative employer rose a little.
Of course, the most important part is still left.
Four days of pay, Tuesday through Friday. My first weekly paycheck as a C-rank Hunter.
Of course I was excited to find out how much it was.
I swallowed and opened my mouth.
“Then how much is all of this...?”
“I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount. The settlement details are inside, so check them. We’ll be going.”
“Until next time, Hunter.”
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim took off in a flash.
It all happened in an instant.
I stared after the receding car lights, bewildered, then opened the drink box. In the faint moonlight, thick bundles of bills caught my eye.
One, two, three...
The count stopped at six.
Six bundles of a hundred bills.
In other words, six million won.
“What is this?”
Scam.
The word flashed through my mind. Just as my legs were about to give out—
“Huh?”
Had I seen it wrong? Why were the bills yellowish?
“Wait. Wait a second!”
I focused internal energy into my eyes, and my vision brightened.
Then I saw her.
A kindly smiling woman in a hanbok, right there on the bill.
“Shin Saimdang! Wise mother and virtuous wife! Her son is Yulgok Yi I! Her husband is Yi Wonsu!”
I started speaking in tongues before I knew it.
This was insane. Completely insane.
One bundle held a hundred Shin Saimdang bills. Six of those meant...
“Th-three hundred million!”
This time I couldn’t catch myself as my legs gave out. I dropped to my knees with a thud and stared blankly into the drink box.
Under the bundles, a white sheet of paper lined the bottom.
Right. The settlement sheet!
I unfolded it in a panic.
It contained a complete record of the past four days’ earnings.
Right down to the final amount being paid to me.
The settlement says thirty million won?
What? Had I imagined it?
I was confused. Completely confused.
My shaking gaze froze on the final line.
Then I remembered Team Leader Choi’s last words before leaving.
I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount.
Thunder and lightning raged through my head.
I rose on trembling legs. Far off in the distance, the car’s lights were already fading.
They looked like a single ray of light.
“Ahh. Aaaah...”
Team Leader Choi.
No—he was the Light.

chapters.title: Chapter 52
paragraphs: Six in the morning.
Taxi driver Mr. Kim picked up his first fare of the day—and regretted it ten minutes later.
What rotten luck.
At first glance, the young man looked perfectly normal. He had a sturdy, muscular build and a clean-cut face. At most, he looked to be in his mid-to-late twenties.
But then...
“Sniff, sniff.”
Something was off about him. Very off.
“Huuugh.”
He was hugging a drink box like treasure, cracking it open every thirty seconds to smell it, then shuddering as if possessed.
What the hell is he doing?
A chill ran down the back of Mr. Kim’s neck. He had been driving a taxi for more than ten years, but he had never encountered this particular breed of problem customer before.
Just as he stole another glance at the young man in the passenger seat—
“Mister.”
“Y-Yes?!”
His heart nearly stopped.
The young man’s eyes, hollow only a moment ago, now gleamed like a wild beast’s.
“There’s a truck behind us.”
“A-a truck? A blue one?”
“Yes. Doesn’t it look like it’s been following us since that intersection?”
“Huh? Well, I suppose it does.”
“It might be tailing us.”
What fresh bullshit was this?
Mr. Kim’s eyes darted around before he finally gave the answer the young man seemed to want.
“I-I’ll peel off to the side.”
The young man hugged the drink box tight until the blue truck disappeared from view, as if someone might snatch it away.
“Sniff. Sniff.”
Of course, he didn’t forget to smell it every chance he got.
This guy’s completely insane.
The AC was blasting inside the car, but Mr. Kim’s back was soaked with cold sweat. And this was his first fare of the day.
What a thoroughly cursed day.
Vroom.
The moment I handed over the fare and shut the door, the taxi shot off like a bullet.
Anyone watching would’ve thought a monster was chasing it. What if he got in an accident?
I clicked my tongue and headed into the apartment complex, still cradling yesterday’s drink box against my chest.
Three hundred million won.
That was about as much as I’d saved over three full years as an F-rank Hunter. Of course, I didn’t have a single won of it left now.
I spent it all paying off debts.
There had been a time when I was drowning in debt, but I’d gritted my teeth and kept going until things gradually got better. I’d even moved my family into a safe-zone apartment near Ilsan.
Lately, though, my life had been like a roller coaster.
A roller coaster that would plummet if the System disappeared...
No. I was home for the first time in months. I needed to stop thinking about that.
Which building and unit was it again?
I only came by once every couple of months, so this always happened.
I glared at the tightly packed apartment buildings, then pulled out my phone and called. It rang for quite a while before the line finally connected.
Click.
“Hello?”
I’d expected Hayeon to still be asleep this early, but her voice was perfectly clear.
“You were already up?”
“Of course I’m up. Do you know what time it is?”
“It’s not even seven.”
“I study better when I wake up early.”
My little sister never failed to impress me. Jinho hyung, who considered waking up in the morning one of the seven deadly sins, should’ve heard that.
“Why’d you call?”
“I’m out front.”
“Huh? Out front?”
“Yeah. But I forgot which one is ours.”
“...Again? You really are something. Wait there.”
I stood there holding the dead phone. A few minutes later, a girl emerged from the entrance of one of the buildings, dragging her slippers along.
Even from a distance, she radiated the aura of a total bum. The look on her face said that everything in the world was too much trouble, and I couldn’t help laughing.
“Jin Hayeon!”
“Don’t yell. You’ll wake people up.”
...Yeah. That was my little sister.
“What brings you here? You didn’t even tell us you were coming.”
“Do I have to announce it before coming to my own house?”
“You show up so rarely. The women’s association president probably visits more often than you do.”
“That bad?”
“That bad.”
The elevator stopped. Hayeon punched in the code at the front door and turned the handle.
And there—
“Son!”
Someone stood beaming at me.
Wrinkled hands. A perm half fallen out. She looked as delighted as a child receiving a surprise gift.
My throat tightened. I scratched my chin, then burst out laughing.
“I’m home, Mom.”
I had finally come back.
To the place where my family was waiting.
Home.
Sizzle, sizzle.
Mom was busy with breakfast in the kitchen. A good smell hung in the air.
“Look at Lady Kim, all excited because her son’s finally home.”
Hayeon scratched her stomach and plopped down beside me.
The old sofa sagged beneath her.
What a pig.
“Is she making a lot?”
“Yeah. A whole feast. Looks like we’re eating well today.”
She answered without taking her eyes off her phone.
“You haven’t seen your brother in ages. Aren’t you happy to see me?”
“Huh?”
“I mean, you could at least massage my shoulders after everything I’ve been through.”
Hayeon let out a long sigh.
“What’s gotten into you, Mr. Taekyung? We don’t have that kind of relationship.”
“...Listen to that attitude.”
It wasn’t like we’d only started bickering yesterday, but I still felt a pang.
I mean, I’d barely made it home after nearly dying!
“That got to you just now, didn’t it?”
Her radar was scary.
“Go get ready for school, you little cafeteria parasite.”
“Mm. Today’s the school founding anniversary.”
My fist trembled.
I wanted to smack the back of her irritating head right then and there, but if I did, I’d really lose.
“You want to hit me, don’t you? Your fist is shaking.”
“You’re lucky you’re a girl. If you had balls, I would’ve—”
“Mom! Oppa’s sexually harassing me!”
“Hey, hey!”
“He said b—mmph!”
I clamped a hand over Hayeon’s mouth. She thrashed, hitting and pinching me, but she was still just a nineteen-year-old girl. It didn’t hurt.
Then one of her flailing feet accidentally slammed into the drink box I’d carefully set in the corner of the sofa.
Thump.
Flutter.
The box sprang wide open.
Yellow bundles of bills spilled across the living-room floor.
Hayeon froze.
“Come on, stop fighting and eat your breakf—”
Mom had come out of the kitchen too.
Everything in the living room stopped as if someone had hit pause. Only the quiet simmering of the stew filled the silence.
Sizzle, sizzle.
I smiled awkwardly and opened my mouth.
“Can’t we talk about this after breakfast?”
“Mmph, mmph, mmph.”
It looked like breakfast would be delayed for quite a while.
I told my family a suitably edited version of everything that had happened so far.
My reawakening as a C-rank Hunter, and where the money had come from.
“So that’s what happened.”
Their reactions fell into two categories.
“I see.”
Mom nodded blankly.
And then—
“Proof.”
Yeah. I hadn’t expected anything else from you.
I sighed and tossed Hayeon my wallet.
“What’s this?”
“Take a look.”
She eyed me suspiciously, then started rummaging through it. There was barely anything inside, so it didn’t take her long to find it.
“Whoa.”
A single card in her hand.
It was the C-rank Hunter license the Association had issued me two days ago.
“This isn’t fake, is it?”
“Want to get hit?”
“Guess it’s real.”
“Forging one is a serious crime, you idiot.”
“What about the money? Did that Team Leader Choi or whatever his name is really give it to you, like you said?”
“How many times do I have to tell you before you believe me?”
“About three hundred and fifty?”
Despite what she said, she seemed to believe me now.
A silver C-rank Hunter license. Three hundred million won in neatly stacked bundles.
Every bit of it looked completely out of place in this old, cramped living room.
Mom sat there staring blankly and muttered, almost a groan.
“What on earth is all this...?”
Hayeon let out a hollow laugh like an old woman who had seen everything life had to offer.
“I know. Live long enough and you see everything.”
“You’re not even twenty.”
“It’s just an expression. But, Mom.”
“Y-Yes?”
“I smell something burning.”
“Oh, right! The stew!”
Mom’s half-lidded eyes flew open. I hurried to my feet, but the kitchen was already a disaster zone.
Mom followed me in, stomping her feet.
“Oh no! What do we do?”
The broth had boiled down to almost nothing, and the fish had turned into lumps of charcoal. I’d been looking forward to a home-cooked meal after so long, but...
Well, this wasn’t such a bad turn of events either.
“Let’s go out to eat. It’s been a while.”
Normally, Mom would’ve launched into a long speech about the absurd price of restaurant food, while Hayeon would’ve asked us to order fried chicken instead. This time, they both stayed quiet.
“Little sister.”
“Yes, dear brother.”
“Grab the money.”
“Yessir.”
As if she’d been waiting for the order, Hayeon swept up the bundles of cash.
“I’m sorry, but our restaurant has a dress code...”
The manager of the upscale restaurant—where a course meal cost several hundred thousand won per person—gave us an awkward smile.
“A dress code?”
“Yes. As you can see, all our other guests are dressed accordingly.”
He was right. Men and women alike wore suits and dresses. Some were even in evening gowns.
Shit. Anyone watching would think they’d come to dance at a ball.
What was this, eighteenth-century France?
For someone like me, who’d only ever gone to gukbap places, it was a massive culture shock.
“Let’s just go somewhere else.”
“Yeah. Hayeon knows a lot of good restaurants around here.”
My family seemed even more embarrassed than I was, so I simply walked out.

The three of us were reflected in the restaurant glass. We’d clearly dressed up for our first meal out in a long time, but every piece we owned was cheap market-brand stuff that already looked well-worn.
Had they been that short on money?
I’d sent most of what I earned home while cutting back on my own food and clothes.
Even when I was an F-rank Hunter, I’d worked twice as hard as everyone else. It couldn’t have been a small amount.
“Son, should we go get pork belly? Maybe something greasy is a bit much this early in the morning.”
“Pork belly sounds good. Mom knows what’s what. A friend of mine went to the barbecue place at the intersection up ahead and said it was amazing.”
Just pork belly.
I had a C-rank Hunter license in my wallet and a bag stuffed with cash. They knew that. They could afford to splurge without worrying.
That’s why I work.
Someone once said money couldn’t buy happiness. That happiness didn’t come with a price tag.
Personally, I had one thing to say to people who spouted that crap.
Fuck off.
You can’t spend money when you don’t have any.
After spending all night wondering what to do with it, I’d finally made up my mind.
For today, at least, I would spare no expense on my family.
And now, that resolve swelled even stronger.
“Let’s eat a little later.”
Without waiting for an answer, I flagged down a passing taxi.
“Where to?”
“Mirae Department Store.”
It was supposedly the biggest and most expensive department store in the area. In the rearview mirror, Mom’s eyes widened.
“The department store?”
Meanwhile, the corners of Hayeon’s mouth curled up slyly.
“Nice. My rich oppa can buy me clothes too.”
Sharp as ever. She caught on immediately.
I gave a short laugh.
“Buy whatever you want.”
“Really?”
“Pick out Mom’s things first.”
“Okay.”
“You’ve got yourself a devoted son, ma’am. Ha ha.”
Only then did Mom smile at the driver’s banter.
“You’re really buying everything?”
“Everything.”

Once I confirmed it one last time, Hayeon tore through the department store like a colt off its reins. She scanned the clothes with a terrifyingly keen eye and moved so fast I started to wonder if she was an Awakened.
At first, Mom looked at the price tags more than the clothes. Before long, though, she started joining in enthusiastically.
“Mom, what do you think of this?”
“Isn’t it too short?”
“This one!”
“That’s nice.”
“This too!”
“That’s pretty. Excuse me, miss—do you have this in one size larger?”
Two hours later, I began to feel a change in my body.
I’m dying.
For reasons I couldn’t explain, I was suffering from extreme shortness of breath and agonizing pain in my legs.
A sense of helplessness comparable to what I’d felt facing Jopil in Murim engulfed my entire body.
“Oppa, how do I look?”
“Ugly. Get lost.”
“Son, try this on.”
“I don’t think I need to. I’ll take it.”
I have no idea how many clothes we bought that day or how much we spent.
All I know is that by the time we finished shopping, one of the department store’s top executives came to see us off.
“Welcome.”
The manager of the restaurant with the strict dress code didn’t even recognize us.
“Wow, I’ve never eaten anything like this before.”
“I know. How do they make the food look so pretty?”
Mom and Hayeon whispered to each other, their cheeks flushed.
We’d spent dozens of times more than the several-hundred-thousand-won course meal just so we could eat it, but not a single won felt wasted that day.
“But I want rice. This is too rich.”
“Why are the portions so small?”
...I pretended not a single won felt wasted.

chapters.title: Chapter 53
paragraphs: Ding.
System Sleep Mode has ended.
“...O-oppa!”
I gasped and opened my eyes.
The first thing I saw wasn’t the ceiling of my goshiwon, but Hayeon’s face.
Oh, right. I came home yesterday.
“Did you have a nightmare?”
“Huh?”
“You were screaming earlier. And you were sweating like crazy.”
I was?
Before I could ask, I realized my whole body was soaked in sweat, and my throat stung as if I’d swallowed sand.
Why do I feel like this?
The System didn’t only work while I was awake. Sleep Mode let me sleep deeply while restoring me to peak condition.
Nothing like this had ever happened in Murim or since Synchronization. And a nightmare, on top of that?
What did I even dream about?
My head throbbed, but I couldn’t remember the dream at all.
Hayeon asked worriedly, “Has something bad happened lately?”
“No. Nothing like that.”
“If there is, tell me. Don’t suffer by yourself.”
“Yes, nuna.”
“I’m not joking.”
Her little fist thumped my chest. Faced with Hayeon’s serious expression, I had nothing to say. I scratched my chin.
“Really? Nothing bothering you? Nothing giving you a hard time?”
“I told you, there’s nothing.”

It was a lie. There had been things seven years ago, and there would be things seven years from now. There had been days when I locked myself in my room and cried, and days when I drank myself senseless with Jinho just to forget.
That’s enough.

There were things I couldn’t tell my mother, who had worked until the cartilage in her knees wore down raising the two of us, or my little sister, a high-school senior now preparing for her college entrance exam.
Enduring things alone and overcoming them. I was used to it by now.
I flashed her a grin as if nothing was wrong.
“My life’s finally about to take off. What would I have to worry about? Ah, there is one thing. How I’m supposed to spend all this money. Something like that.”
“Big talk.”
The mood lightened a little. I made a face on purpose.
“Big talk? Don’t you remember yesterday? Want me to show you the bundles of cash again?”
“I’ll give you that. You’re obnoxious, but I can’t argue.”
“I’ve hit the peak of my twenty-seven-year life graph. Nothing’s going on, so you just study hard.”
“My grades are in the top 0.1 percent nationwide, okay? I’m doing more than well enough, so don’t worry.”
Hayeon pouted and started to leave, then stopped and turned back.
“Oppa. But...”
“Yeah?”
“Who’s Jin Wikyung?”
“...What?”
A name I never expected, at a moment like this.
My body went rigid.
Crunch.
I bit into a piece of freshly made young-radish kimchi. It was Mom’s cooking, the food I’d wanted so badly, but I could barely taste it.
Because of the conversation I’d just had with Hayeon.
“Where did you hear that name?”
“From you. You kept saying it in your sleep.”
And then her final question.
“Someone you know? If they show up in your dreams, you must be close.”
I couldn’t answer. I hadn’t found that answer in Murim or in reality.
No. I no longer had any reason to look for it. I had returned to reality, and Jin Wikyung was in Murim.
Then why did Jin Wikyung suddenly show up in my dream...?
My thoughts were a mess. Was it some aftereffect of Murim? The term PTSD came to mind—post-traumatic stress disorder.
This is driving me crazy.
My expression must have hardened without my noticing. Mom asked gently, “Have you lost your appetite? I made all your favorites.”
“Oh, no. When did you make the kimchi? And this doenjang-jjigae is perfect.”
I hurriedly made excuses and picked up my spoon. For the first time in ages, the three of us were together at one table. I couldn’t ruin this precious moment.
It’s nothing. It has to be nothing.
Slurp.

The unease nagging at the back of my mind soon faded, and I went back to normal.
I laughed and talked with my family all day. I even took a long nap, and by the time I woke up, it was evening.
Time to go back.

“There goes Lady Kim again. I know how to eat boiled pork too, you know?”
Hayeon grumbled at the reluctance dripping from Mom’s words.
“She packed you a ton of side dishes already, so why are you so worried? At this rate, she could open a side-dish shop.”
“...That’s true.”
The shopping bags Mom had prepared by the front door were packed with side dishes. Even this much was a compromise I’d only managed to reach after talking her down.
I don’t have anywhere to put them.
If I put a fridge in my three-pyeong goshiwon room, there really wouldn’t be anywhere left to stand. No—there wasn’t even room for a fridge.
I already had a capsule the size of one.
Should I start looking for a new place?
I was thinking that as I slung the backpack I’d packed the night before over my shoulder.
Why was it so heavy? All I’d put inside were a few outfits I’d bought yesterday.
When I set the backpack down, my family suddenly grew frantic.
“Son, you’ll be busy starting tomorrow, right? Hurry back, wash up, and get a good night’s sleep.”
“...A minute ago, you told me to stay a few more days.”
“Oppa, you’re going to miss your ride.”
“I’m taking a taxi, though?”
“The late-night surcharge. You’ll have to pay the late-night surcharge.”
By then, I had a pretty good idea what was going on.
“When did you put it in?”
“P-put what in?”
“The money.”
Their faces answered for them. I sighed.
“I told you to keep it and use it when you need it.”
“I make plenty of money. And I will from now on, too.”
I mixed fact and fiction fifty-fifty.

That was why I’d wanted to give even more to my family, but...

“Mom.”
“Son.”

Vroom.

“Anyway, don’t touch it. Got it?”
“You look ready to beat me to death.”
“I’ll tear you to pieces.”
I ignored Jinho’s baffled expression and flopped onto the bed.

“Something going on?”
“Going on, my ass.”
“Complaints about you have been no joke lately. Today, I barely managed to calm down the guy next door and send him away.”

Jinho gathered up the tools he’d scattered across the floor and continued.

That name again.
I buried my face in the pillow.
“Just tell him she’s my girlfriend.”
I saw his hand tremble around the monkey wrench.
“You got a girlfriend? You traitorous bastard.”
“Is she pretty? How old is she? Show me a picture.”
This guy was thirty. It was tragic.
“The name’s a bit exotic, though. Is she an ethnic Korean from China? Or Chinese?”
“...Chinese.”
It wasn’t exactly wrong.
“This bastard hits C-rank and he’s already gone global. Anyway, introduce me to a girl. I like China. Nǐ hǎo ma? Wǒ ài nǐ. What else was there?”
“You fucking bastard.”
“Idiot. You got the tones and pronunciation all wrong. You think you’ll even make it to a hundred days like that? Repeat after me. Nǐ chī fàn le ma?”
“You fucking bastard.”
“Again. Nǐ chī fàn le ma?”
“You fucking bastard.”
“...Wait, you bastard!”
I ignored Jinho, enraged by his belated realization, and pointed at the door.
“Get out.”
Please. Just let me have some time to myself.
Once the room was quiet, I sat up and walked over to the capsule. I tapped its old, grime-caked surface and muttered, “What the hell are you?”
As expected, no answer came.
I’d secretly been hoping for one. What a shame.
The System’s already synchronized with reality. Why couldn’t a machine talk too?
Honestly, I wasn’t even sure it was a real machine. Reality had turned into fantasy a long time ago, but wasn’t this a whole new genre?
If I wrote my current situation as a novel, what genre would I even pick? Fantasy? A game novel? Or—
Dimensional travel?
A hollow laugh escaped me. Dimensional travel? I really was losing it. There was no way something like that was possible.
There was no way...
My mind snapped clear as if someone had dumped ice water over my head.
...It is possible.
Dimensional travel had happened in the past, and it still existed now.
The invasion of the Demon King Asmodeus and the Gates were proof.
We only passed through Gates to leave and return to our world, but decades ago, an army of monsters had crossed through one from another dimension to Earth.
The Demon Realm.
A land of evil. The home of monsters. The Demon King’s domain.
An unknown dimension no human had ever set foot in or even glimpsed. That was how humanity defined it.
But what if this capsule in front of me was a kind of Gate leading to another dimension? What if Murim was another unknown dimension?
Murim is another reality.
Everything I had seen and experienced there.
Water. Earth. Wind. And people, too.
They weren’t NPCs.
I stared at my vacant face reflected on the capsule’s faded surface.
For a long while after that.

chapters.title: Chapter 54
paragraphs: It felt like watching an old TV.
Scenes and voices stuttered across a faded screen, cutting in and out. Even so, the heat of the battlefield came through vividly.
“Kill them!”
“Destroy the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
The people packed into the narrow gorge charged forward with a roar. Behind them, a flag marked Mount Heng whipped in the air.
Beyond the points of their blue-edged weapons stood another banner.
Jin (振).
And hundreds of martial artists sealing off the gorge.
“They’re bastards with neither martial honor nor chivalry. The Mount Heng Sword Sect disappears today!”
“Attack!”
Static crackled.
The view zoomed in through the noise, locking onto two people who stood out beneath the flag of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
An old man with a long white beard spoke.
“This will be a long fight.”
A massive man answered.
“And our last.”
The old man broke into a broad smile.
“It will be. Without fail.”
Then—
People crashed into people, swords into spears. Countless martial artists collided, and a thick mist of blood settled over the gorge.
Somewhere, drums thundered to announce the start of the battle.
Boom. Boom. Boom.
“Hah.”
I sat up, drenched in sweat. Another dream about Murim.
Unlike at first, I could now remember the dream clearly even after waking.
The battle has begun.
Time continued to pass in Murim even after I returned to reality.
The scenes I had just witnessed might be happening there right now. A great battle with the fate of two immense powers hanging in the balance.
No. There’s one more.
A third force led by the Head Elder.
Once the battle reached its climax and both sides had suffered heavy losses, that was when they would finally move.
What about Hyuk Mujin? What happened to the reconnaissance squad?
If they arrived in time and exposed the betrayal, the worst could still be avoided. Or they might already be too late, and everything might be over.
The Head Elder...
An old man who had given me the creeps from the first impression. Who would have thought that so-called elder of the Jin Family of Taiyuan would be plotting something like this?
If the Head Elder emerged as the final victor, it would all be over.
A rebellion was always followed by a bloody purge.
Jin Wikyung, Wipeng, Hyuk Mujin, and the reconnaissance squad.
Then there was Han Yeop, too badly injured in his fight with Jopil to march out, as well as Gong Yacheong and the siblings Socheon and Soyul, who were still recovering.
Familiar faces appeared and vanished in my mind, over and over.
What were they to me?
One month in Murim.
To them, I had been a Benefactor, a trusted superior, and a comrade they could trust to watch their backs. And to someone...
“I’m proud of you.”
“Are you hurt anywhere?”
“Survive, my youngest.”
We were also brothers by blood.
But what had they been to me? NPCs loaded with advanced AI? Or people?
What were they?
Another dimension only I could come and go from, and the people left behind there. What was I supposed to do about that?
My eyes drifted to the capsule on their own.
What if I went back...?
The thought startled me.
I was out of my mind.
Go back and do what? This was a massive battle involving some two thousand martial artists. Among them were monsters as strong as Jopil, One Question, One Kill—or even stronger.
And I was thinking of going back there?
“You lunatic. You crazy bastard. You’ve completely lost it.”
I was muttering the words like a sigh when my phone buzzed.
Bzzz.
Designer-Brand Junkie.
It was Team Leader Choi.
A large café surrounded by downtown skyscrapers.
“Here are the materials you requested.”
Butler Kim held out a thick binder. Even at a glance, it looked like a massive file of more than a hundred pages.
“That’s a lot.”
“I investigated just as thoroughly.”
Choi Minwoo nodded and began flipping rapidly through the pages. What he was reading was one man’s life.
Jin Taekyung’s twenty-seven years were contained in those hundred-odd pages.
Birthplace, background, how he had grown up—even account inquiry records provided by the bank. Nothing was missing.
Anything unusual or suspicious had been marked in bold, allowing Choi Minwoo to finish the entire file in under thirty minutes.
“What do you think, Butler Kim?”
“He’s clean.”
Butler Kim’s answer was definitive.
“He isn’t an illegal Awakener, nor did he approach you as part of some scheme.”
Choi Minwoo nodded. If Butler Kim said so, then it was so.
Butler Kim had spent the past two weeks using every means available to investigate everything about Jin Taekyung. Every one of the hundred-odd pages on the table would have passed through his hands.
“So this was all a coincidence?”
“For now, yes.”
“Butler Kim.”
“Yes. Please go ahead.”
“Do you know the odds of reawakening?”
“I understand they’re around one percent.”
One in a hundred.
To an ordinary person, that might not sound impossibly rare. But those hundred people weren’t ordinary people. They were Hunters who had already beaten similar odds just to Awaken in the first place.
And even among them, only a chosen few were lucky enough to reawaken.
“Then what are the odds of an F-rank Hunter reawakening as a C-rank Hunter in one leap?”
Choi Minwoo didn’t wait for an answer.
“And what are the odds of a C-rank Hunter clearing a Gate of the same rank alone?”
“Alone, it would be impossible. He would have to be at least B-rank...”
“And yet there’s someone who can.”
“Could it be...?”
“Ten C-rank Gates and ten D-rank Gates. Across twenty raids, all I did was stand by with my arms crossed and watch. There was never any need for me to step in.”
His long fingers tapped the thick binder.
Everything about Jin Taekyung was written inside it, yet in another sense, it said nothing at all.
After a moment of silence, Butler Kim spoke.
“I’ll investigate him again.”
“No.”
Choi Minwoo shook his head.
“Keep poking at it and we’ll only make trouble for ourselves. I intend to keep him close and watch him.”
“Do you intend to recruit him into the Guild after all?”
“I should. If something smells fishy, I’ll dig into his background. If not...”
Choi Minwoo’s eyes gleamed.
“I’ll make him one of my people. Even if it takes Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.”
And in the next moment—
Jingle.
The doorbell rang as someone entered the café, and Choi Minwoo gave a quiet laugh.
Zhuge Liang—or rather, Jin Taekyung.
A signing bonus of 500 million won.
A fixed monthly salary of 50 million won and a seventy-percent settlement share.

An officetel of roughly 132 square meters and a sedan came as extras, while coverage under all four national insurance programs was a given. After reading through the contract, I had exactly one thought.
This is insane.
What kind of outrageous terms were these?
They were giving me a home, a car, and more money than I knew what to do with.
The average annual income of a C-rank Hunter was 200 million won, including fixed pay and raid earnings.
And me?
The signing bonus alone is 500 million.
These terms were normally reserved for B-rank Hunters or higher.
That meant they valued my skills that highly. It was also proof that I had found an employer with enough insight not to judge a Hunter by rank alone.
And he has the money to back it up.
I stared across the table at Team Leader Choi. As always, his expression gave nothing away, and his eyes were deep.
Team Leader Choi suddenly spoke.
“This is the third time.”
He had made me two offers before, and I had turned them both down. This was his roundabout way of telling me not to refuse him again.
“I’m sorry about that. There was a minor issue.”
“Have you resolved it?”
“Yes. For now, I think so.”
“Then there shouldn’t be any problem now.”
“...Of course.”
Even as I answered, doubt gnawed at me.
Was there really no problem now? Was it okay to leave things like this?
What the hell am I thinking?
I needed to get this over with before my thoughts wandered again.
“I’ll sign.”
I began signing with the fountain pen Team Leader Choi had handed me.
One page, two pages, three...
The contract was five pages long. All I had to do was write the three characters of my name on the last page, and it would be done.
At that moment, the question returned.
Is this really okay?
The fountain pen that had moved without hesitation began to slow. One thought led to another.
What if it isn’t? But isn’t this exactly what I wanted?
It was.
This was what I had desperately dreamed of for seven years.
A massive salary and high social standing.
Becoming a son and older brother my family could be proud of, and giving them a comfortable life.
Becoming someone others envied and admired instead of ignored and looked down on.
I can have it all now.
I could spend the rest of my life enjoying all of it. Goodbye to my miserable old life. Goodbye to that shitty Murim.
Crack.
And goodbye to the fountain pen, too.
I relaxed my grip. Ink spilled from the shattered pen and soaked into the contract.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. Let me ask you again.”
Team Leader Choi pulled out a white handkerchief and wiped the ink that had splashed onto his chin.
Despite the sudden mess, he looked perfectly calm.
“That problem from last time. Have you really resolved it?”
“No.”
The moment I answered, I felt a weight lift from my chest.
“If it’s something I can help you with...”
“I appreciate the offer, but I have to handle this myself.”
Team Leader Choi studied me with an odd look, then gave a quiet laugh.
“I didn’t know signing a contract could be this difficult. I never expected to be turned down three times, either.”
He sounded more amused by the situation than angry.
“When would be a good time for the fourth offer?”
He had probably meant it half as a joke, but my answer was serious.
“Tomorrow. Same time, same place.”
“Tomorrow?”
“Yes. Tomorrow.”
Only one day.
But for me, it would be a month, or perhaps several.
Team Leader Choi had no way of knowing that, and he furrowed his brow.
“I don’t much like jokes like that.”
“Neither do I. Not jokes like this.”
He had no idea what my words meant.
“I’ll be sure to see you.”
It was a vow to myself.
A vow that I would return alive.
And...
“Tomorrow, you’ll have to raise the contract terms even further.”
I left the café, leaving Team Leader Choi behind with his eyes wide.
“Phew.”
I took a deep breath and opened the capsule.
The sight of the sagging seat and VR headset made my heart pound. Even after coming this far, temptation kept rearing its head and whispering to me.
Don’t go back.
Forget everything and be satisfied with your life here.
Everyone you met in Murim was an NPC, and Murim is nothing more than a game.
Right. There had been a time when I thought that way.
But after wrestling with it, I realized that one way or another, I was going back.
I’d already reached my conclusion a long time ago.
On the night of the blizzard, I had gone back for Gong Yacheong.
I had brought along two young siblings who were nothing but baggage, and instead of using the reconnaissance squad as shields, I had fought Jopil and nearly died.
It probably started then.
That was when the three letters NPC, lodged in my mind, began to fade.
That was when I saw the two-character word for family in Jin Wikyung’s back as he told me to survive and turned away.
“Fuck. My life really is a variety show.”
With a hollow, complaining laugh, I climbed into the capsule. The moment I put on the VR headset, a single line of text appeared in front of me.
Ding.
System Would you like to log in to Murim? Accept / Decline
“Yes.”
My consciousness faded. My vision went dark.
I logged in.

NPCs loaded with advanced AI?

Another dimension only I could come and go from, and the people left behind there.

My eyes drifted to the capsule on their own.

The thought startled me.
I was out of my mind.
Go back and do what?
This was a massive battle involving some two thousand martial artists.

And I was thinking of going back there?

I was muttering the words like a sigh when my phone buzzed.
Bzzz.
Designer-Brand Junkie.
It was Team Leader Choi.
A large café surrounded by downtown skyscrapers.
“Here are the materials you requested.”
Butler Kim held out a thick binder.
Even at a glance, it looked like a massive file of more than a hundred pages.
“That’s a lot.”
“I investigated just as thoroughly.”
Choi Minwoo nodded and began flipping rapidly through the pages.
What he was reading was one man’s life.
Jin Taekyung’s twenty-seven years were contained in those hundred-odd pages.
Birthplace, background, how he had grown up—even account inquiry records provided by the bank.
Nothing was missing.
Anything unusual or suspicious had been marked in bold, allowing Choi Minwoo to finish the entire file in under thirty minutes.

“He’s clean.”
Butler Kim’s answer was definitive.
“He isn’t an illegal Awakener, nor did he approach you as part of some scheme.”
Choi Minwoo nodded.
If Butler Kim said so, then it was so.
Butler Kim had spent the past two weeks using every means available to investigate everything about Jin Taekyung.
Every one of the hundred-odd pages on the table would have passed through his hands.
“So this was all a coincidence?”
“For now, yes.”
“Butler Kim.”
“Yes.
Please go ahead.”

“I understand they’re around one percent.”
One in a hundred.
To an ordinary person, that might not sound impossibly rare.
But those hundred people weren’t ordinary people.
They were Hunters who had already beaten similar odds just to Awaken in the first place.
And even among them, only a chosen few were lucky enough to reawaken.

Choi Minwoo didn’t wait for an answer.
