chapters.title: Chapter 55
paragraphs: This is driving me crazy.
Hyuk Mujin felt the world go yellow before his eyes.
Assassins disguised as disciples of minor sects. The Head Elder’s betrayal. That alone was enough to make his head explode, but...
Why the hell did this guy collapse too?!
Jin Taekyung had passed out without warning. The reconnaissance squad members had taken turns slapping his cheeks and shaking him by the collar, but he still showed no sign of waking.
He’s definitely still breathing.
It was enough to make a ghost weep. And with things as they were, Hyuk Mujin—the deputy squad leader—had ended up in charge of this enormous mess.
“You, and you.”
Mujin singled out two of the reconnaissance squad members still standing there in a daze.
“Return to the main family at once and report what happened.”
The Head Elder.
Mujin did not know why one of the family’s most respected elders, a hero of the old Great Faction War, had devised such a dark scheme or what he hoped to gain from it.
But they had to prevent the worst from coming to pass.
“The rest of us are heading for the main force. Hurry!”
Mujin hoisted the unconscious Jin Taekyung onto his back.
After running for roughly two hours, the world went yellow before his eyes again—this time for a different reason.
I’m going to die.

It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries. He had boasted to Jin Taekyung that he was almost fully recovered, but in truth, he needed at least two solid weeks of rest.
“Huff... huff.”
He was soaked through, and his legs were trembling.
He would have fallen behind even if he had only been trying to keep up. With the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back, he was practically dying.
Ah, Mother. Father.
Now he was even hallucinating his parents—who were alive and well—beckoning to him. The woman standing beside them had a face he often saw in the temple hall.
Guanyin Bodhisattva?
“Child. You have suffered enough. You may rest now.”
Her benevolent smile slowly put Mujin’s heart at ease.
Yeah. I’ve done enough. The squad leader drops like a rock when it matters most, and these bastards won’t even offer to carry him for me, whether I drop dead or not.
Fuck it. Whatever.
Mujin was just about to let go when—
“Whew... haaah.”
Warm breath slipped into his ear. He knew who it was without turning around. Tears of relief stung Hyuk’s eyes.
“Captain!”
Jin Taekyung grinned and whispered,
“Candy in your ear.”
Clang! Clang!
“Kill them! Kill them!”
“Graaah!”
Blood sprayed and screams rang out on every side. A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.
His still-youthful face was stained with pain and terror.
“Hnnh... hhhk...”
He tried to hold it back, but the sobs kept breaking free. He had spent ten years gritting his teeth and honing his martial arts, yet none of it had helped him on this blood-soaked battlefield.
The senior he had relied on was dead. So was the fellow disciple who had been like a brother. Weapons had poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.
“Mother... Mother...”
He called for her over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.
Shunk—!
A spearhead protruded from his chest.
His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.
“What’s a brat doing here?”
But even a wandering martial artist who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him a moment later.
Slice—
A silver line flashed, and the wandering martial artist’s head shot into the air.
A wandering martial artist killed a martial artist. Another martial artist killed the wandering martial artist.
Nameless men killed and died on every side, over and over.
That was what a battlefield was.
Yes. This was what it was like.
The Head Elder gazed over the battlefield, lost in memory.
Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago. How many people had died in that narrow gorge?
I was young then, too.
His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. Back then, the embarrassing word chivalry had still meant so much to him.
But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.
What good is a chivalrous warrior? Die, and you’re nothing but a ghost.
That realization had been a form of enlightenment. In the end, he had survived and become a hero. After long years of patient endurance, he had finally reached this point.
Now it was time to reap the fruit.
The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.
What a waste. Such a waste.

Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps that was also why he was so deeply respected within the family.
He is more than capable of restoring this family.
If Jin Wikyung became the Family Head, and if his two younger brothers—each already distinguishing himself—stood firmly behind him...
The Head Elder caught himself and let out a short laugh.
What a ridiculous thing to be thinking after coming this far. Besides, Jin Taekyung was probably already dead, reduced to a lonely ghost.
“I’ve grown old.”
Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet mutter.
“Did you say something?”
“Nothing of importance. Old men tend to talk to themselves. More importantly, how does the battle look to you, Lesser Family Head?”
“It is going in our favor, but...”
Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.
There was no way he could watch members of his family die and feel at ease.
“Lesser Family Head. I understand how you feel, but do not act rashly.”
The Head Elder’s warning was stern.
“A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient the enemy will become. That is the moment we must seize.”
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon throw its full strength at us.”
“They’ll put their Peak masters at the front. Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”
“Then everything will be decided.”
The Head Elder nodded.
“If you, Wipeng, and I hold off the enemy commanders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will collapse.”
“It’s a shame we can’t use fire. I resent the heavens.”
The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.
Yet even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, what he hoped for would never have happened.
The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s command.
“I resent the heavens as well.”
The Head Elder meant it.
He had waited far too many years. He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.
“Candy in your ear.”
“Captain!”
“Was it sweet as a dream?”
“...Are you insane?”
The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face filled me with relief. I felt the same way about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around after hearing I was awake.
“Captain’s awake!”
“What happened? Are you all right?”
“Wasn’t he dead?”
I’d have to deal with the bastard who had just said that later. I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.
“Been a while. You guys been well?”
“Huh?”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“Did he hit his head?”
“His head—check his head!”
Exactly the reaction I’d expected.
Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.
...Not that they didn’t treat me like a lunatic afterward.
“Anyway, that’s enough greeting. How long was I out?”
Mujin sank to the ground with a thud and answered.
“Definitely more than an hour, but probably a little under two.”
I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on to my next question.
“Was I breathing?”
“Why are you asking that all of a sudden? Seriously.”
“We don’t have time. Just answer.”
“You were breathing, so you woke up. Otherwise, you’d be dead.”
Fair enough.
Apparently, logging in or out left my body on the other side in a state of suspended animation.
If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left for me to return to.
I’d think about that later.
There was a more urgent problem.
“The main force?”
“We were already heading toward them. I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”
“Good. How much farther?”
“At least another two hours.”
“Two hours...”
“Uh, Captain. I’m sorry to say this, but... I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”
Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent. Nobody had to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.
I’ve thought about it too.
According to what Gwak Jun had said just before he died, this betrayal had been meticulously planned for a long time.
But the plan had exactly one flaw.
Me.
The Head Elder had underestimated me.
No—maybe in a way, he had overestimated me. He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.
Even that hadn’t been enough. I had survived.
He made a mistake.
On top of that, when Gwak Jun first revealed his true colors, he’d said they needed to get moving soon if they wanted to arrive on time.
Which meant...
“It’s not too late.”
I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.
“Don’t think about the worst-case scenario. No matter what it takes, I’ll change that outcome.”
“Captain...”
“So, Mujin.”
I gave Mujin’s choked-up face a good-natured smile.
“Get up. Now.”
“I’m dying here.”
“Want to get beaten to death instead?”
“Run even one more step in the time we’ve got. Don’t you know marathon spirit?”
“I don’t.”
Ah. Right. This was Murim.
“Anyway, get up. Another hour will do it.”
Mujin grabbed his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.
“An hour?”
“Yeah. An hour.”
“I already told you. Even at full speed, it’ll take two hours.”
“Exactly. An hour.”
“What are you even talking about...?”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
Mujin blinked at me with the guileless eyes of an ox. I smiled even brighter.
“You ever heard of grit?”
I didn’t care whether it should take two hours or four.
We were getting there in one hour. Period.
“Run like hell. That’ll do it.”
“Huk.”
Every face in the reconnaissance squad went deathly pale.
“We’ve been blocked.”
“Casualties are mounting. Sect Leader, please take action.”
Even as the reports continued, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, did not open his eyes.
I was too hasty.
The war had started in a rush, and the preparations had been just as thin. Provisions were burning down fast, morale was dropping, and deserters were popping up one after another.
They read us completely.
Rage over his son’s death and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.
And so he had encountered the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name had been unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.
“Sect Leader!”
At his subordinate’s shout, Lee Cheonbaek slowly opened his eyes.
The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.
“Gaaah!”
“Wipe them out! They’re nothing but rabble!”

Well over a thousand of his men were trapped at the narrow entrance, unable to advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.
Sword fodder, at best.
Just as he clicked his tongue inwardly, several dozen wandering martial artists began peeling away from the front line. The middle-aged wanderer leading them shouted at the top of his lungs.
“This is a dog’s death! Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”
Those became the middle-aged wandering martial artist’s last words.
Whoosh—
A light breeze.
That was all the wanderer felt.
He did not know that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already brushed past him. He did not know that the wandering martial artists under him had frozen in terror.
He only thought, all of a sudden, that his neck felt hot.
His cleanly severed head dropped with a dull thunk. The headless body staggered a few more steps, then went down like a rotten old tree.
“Blood Rain Group, was it?”
Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the frozen wanderers. Not a single drop of blood stained the blade.
“Go back.”
A Peak master’s killing intent shot into them like a blade. The wandering martial artists charged toward the front even faster than they had come.
They had decided that fighting at the front beat throwing themselves at the Peak master in front of them.
“Rat bastards.”
Lee Cheonbaek went after them. His burning gaze was aimed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s command had to be.
“The Sect Leader is taking the lead!”
“Everyone, charge! Wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
As Lee Cheonbaek stepped forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.
Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters surged toward the front.

sentences.text: This is driving me crazy.
Hyuk Mujin felt the world go yellow before his eyes.
Assassins disguised as disciples of minor sects.
The Head Elder’s betrayal.
That alone was enough to make his head explode, but...
Why the hell did this guy collapse too?!
Jin Taekyung had passed out without warning.
The reconnaissance squad members had taken turns slapping his cheeks and shaking him by the collar, but he still showed no sign of waking.
He’s definitely still breathing.
It was enough to make a ghost weep.
And with things as they were, Hyuk Mujin—the deputy squad leader—had ended up in charge of this enormous mess.
“You, and you.”
Mujin singled out two of the reconnaissance squad members still standing there in a daze.
“Return to the main family at once and report what happened.”
The Head Elder.
Mujin did not know why one of the family’s most respected elders, a hero of the old Great Faction War, had devised such a dark scheme or what he hoped to gain from it.
But they had to prevent the worst from coming to pass.
“The rest of us are heading for the main force.
Hurry!”
Mujin hoisted the unconscious Jin Taekyung onto his back.
After running for roughly two hours, the world went yellow before his eyes again—this time for a different reason.
I’m going to die.
It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries.
He had boasted to Jin Taekyung that he was almost fully recovered, but in truth, he needed at least two solid weeks of rest.
“Huff... huff.”
He was soaked through, and his legs were trembling.
He would have fallen behind even if he had only been trying to keep up.
With the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back, he was practically dying.
Ah, Mother.
Father.
Now he was even hallucinating his parents—who were alive and well—beckoning to him.
The woman standing beside them had a face he often saw in the temple hall.
Guanyin Bodhisattva?
“Child.
You have suffered enough.
You may rest now.”
Her benevolent smile slowly put Mujin’s heart at ease.
Yeah.
I’ve done enough.
The squad leader drops like a rock when it matters most, and these bastards won’t even offer to carry him for me, whether I drop dead or not.
Fuck it.
Whatever.
Mujin was just about to let go when—
“Whew... haaah.”
Warm breath slipped into his ear.
He knew who it was without turning around.
Tears of relief stung Hyuk’s eyes.
“Captain!”
Jin Taekyung grinned and whispered,
“Candy in your ear.”
Clang!
Clang!
“Kill them!
Kill them!”
“Graaah!”
Blood sprayed and screams rang out on every side.
A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.
His still-youthful face was stained with pain and terror.
“Hnnh... hhhk...”
He tried to hold it back, but the sobs kept breaking free.
He had spent ten years gritting his teeth and honing his martial arts, yet none of it had helped him on this blood-soaked battlefield.
The senior he had relied on was dead.
So was the fellow disciple who had been like a brother.
Weapons had poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.
“Mother...
Mother...”
He called for her over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.
Shunk—!
A spearhead protruded from his chest.
His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them.
A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.
“What’s a brat doing here?”
But even a wandering martial artist who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him a moment later.
Slice—
A silver line flashed, and the wandering martial artist’s head shot into the air.
A wandering martial artist killed a martial artist.
Another martial artist killed the wandering martial artist.
Nameless men killed and died on every side, over and over.
That was what a battlefield was.
Yes.
This was what it was like.
The Head Elder gazed over the battlefield, lost in memory.
Eight Spring Gorge.
A battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago.
How many people had died in that narrow gorge?
I was young then, too.
His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot.
Back then, the embarrassing word chivalry had still meant so much to him.
But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder.
He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.
What good is a chivalrous warrior?
Die, and you’re nothing but a ghost.
That realization had been a form of enlightenment.
In the end, he had survived and become a hero.
After long years of patient endurance, he had finally reached this point.
Now it was time to reap the fruit.
The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.
What a waste.
Such a waste.
Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent.
He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment a leader needed.
He sometimes allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps that was also why he was so deeply respected within the family.
He is more than capable of restoring this family.
If Jin Wikyung became the Family Head, and if his two younger brothers—each already distinguishing himself—stood firmly behind him...
The Head Elder caught himself and let out a short laugh.
What a ridiculous thing to be thinking after coming this far.
Besides, Jin Taekyung was probably already dead, reduced to a lonely ghost.
“I’ve grown old.”
Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet mutter.
“Did you say something?”
“Nothing of importance.
Old men tend to talk to themselves.
More importantly, how does the battle look to you, Lesser Family Head?”
“It is going in our favor, but...”
Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly.
They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.
There was no way he could watch members of his family die and feel at ease.
“Lesser Family Head.
I understand how you feel, but do not act rashly.”
The Head Elder’s warning was stern.
“A leader must know when to step forward.
The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient the enemy will become.
That is the moment we must seize.”
“The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon throw its full strength at us.”
“They’ll put their Peak masters at the front.
Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”
“Then everything will be decided.”
The Head Elder nodded.
“If you, Wipeng, and I hold off the enemy commanders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will collapse.”
“It’s a shame we can’t use fire.
I resent the heavens.”
The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.
Yet even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, what he hoped for would never have happened.
The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s command.
“I resent the heavens as well.”
The Head Elder meant it.
He had waited far too many years.
He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.
“Candy in your ear.”
“Captain!”
“Was it sweet as a dream?”
“...Are you insane?”
The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face filled me with relief.
I felt the same way about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around after hearing I was awake.
“Captain’s awake!”
“What happened?
Are you all right?”
“Wasn’t he dead?”
I’d have to deal with the bastard who had just said that later.
I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.
“Been a while.
You guys been well?”
“Huh?”
“What’s that supposed to mean?”
“Did he hit his head?”
“His head—check his head!”
Exactly the reaction I’d expected.
Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.
...Not that they didn’t treat me like a lunatic afterward.
“Anyway, that’s enough greeting.
How long was I out?”
Mujin sank to the ground with a thud and answered.
“Definitely more than an hour, but probably a little under two.”
I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up.
I nodded and moved on to my next question.
“Was I breathing?”
“Why are you asking that all of a sudden?
Seriously.”
“We don’t have time.
Just answer.”
“You were breathing, so you woke up.
Otherwise, you’d be dead.”
Fair enough.
Apparently, logging in or out left my body on the other side in a state of suspended animation.
If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left for me to return to.
I’d think about that later.
There was a more urgent problem.
“The main force?”
“We were already heading toward them.
I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”
“Good.
How much farther?”
“At least another two hours.”
“Two hours...”
“Uh, Captain.
I’m sorry to say this, but...
I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”
Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent.
Nobody had to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.
I’ve thought about it too.
According to what Gwak Jun had said just before he died, this betrayal had been meticulously planned for a long time.
But the plan had exactly one flaw.
Me.
The Head Elder had underestimated me.
No—maybe in a way, he had overestimated me.
He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.
Even that hadn’t been enough.
I had survived.
He made a mistake.
On top of that, when Gwak Jun first revealed his true colors, he’d said they needed to get moving soon if they wanted to arrive on time.
Which meant...
“It’s not too late.”
I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.
“Don’t think about the worst-case scenario.
No matter what it takes, I’ll change that outcome.”
“Captain...”
“So, Mujin.”
I gave Mujin’s choked-up face a good-natured smile.
“Get up.
Now.”
“I’m dying here.”
“Want to get beaten to death instead?”
“Run even one more step in the time we’ve got.
Don’t you know marathon spirit?”
“I don’t.”
Ah.
Right.
This was Murim.
“Anyway, get up.
Another hour will do it.”
Mujin grabbed his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.
“An hour?”
“Yeah.
An hour.”
“I already told you.
Even at full speed, it’ll take two hours.”
“Exactly.
An hour.”
“What are you even talking about...?”
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
Mujin blinked at me with the guileless eyes of an ox.
I smiled even brighter.
“You ever heard of grit?”
I didn’t care whether it should take two hours or four.
We were getting there in one hour.
Period.
“Run like hell.
That’ll do it.”
“Huk.”
Every face in the reconnaissance squad went deathly pale.
“We’ve been blocked.”
“Casualties are mounting.
Sect Leader, please take action.”
Even as the reports continued, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, did not open his eyes.
I was too hasty.
The war had started in a rush, and the preparations had been just as thin.
Provisions were burning down fast, morale was dropping, and deserters were popping up one after another.
They read us completely.
Rage over his son’s death and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment.
He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.
And so he had encountered the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name had been unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.
“Sect Leader!”
At his subordinate’s shout, Lee Cheonbaek slowly opened his eyes.
The formidable eyesight of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.
“Gaaah!”
“Wipe them out!
They’re nothing but rabble!”
Well over a thousand of his men were trapped at the narrow entrance, unable to advance.
The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.
Sword fodder, at best.
Just as he clicked his tongue inwardly, several dozen wandering martial artists began peeling away from the front line.
The middle-aged wanderer leading them shouted at the top of his lungs.
“This is a dog’s death!
Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”
Those became the middle-aged wandering martial artist’s last words.
Whoosh—
A light breeze.
That was all the wanderer felt.
He did not know that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already brushed past him.
He did not know that the wandering martial artists under him had frozen in terror.
He only thought, all of a sudden, that his neck felt hot.
His cleanly severed head dropped with a dull thunk.
The headless body staggered a few more steps, then went down like a rotten old tree.
“Blood Rain Group, was it?”
Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the frozen wanderers.
Not a single drop of blood stained the blade.
“Go back.”
A Peak master’s killing intent shot into them like a blade.
The wandering martial artists charged toward the front even faster than they had come.
They had decided that fighting at the front beat throwing themselves at the Peak master in front of them.
“Rat bastards.”
Lee Cheonbaek went after them.
His burning gaze was aimed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s command had to be.
“The Sect Leader is taking the lead!”
“Everyone, charge!
Wipe out the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
As Lee Cheonbaek stepped forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.
Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters surged toward the front.

chapters.title: Chapter 56
paragraphs: The Head Elder was the first to notice Lee Cheonbaek’s arrival.
The leader himself has entered the fray.
The fierce wave of qi blasting across the gorge, and the killing intent rolling with it, made that obvious even without seeing him.
Sure enough—
“You bastards!”
Lee Cheonbaek appeared with a thunderous roar. His half-gray hair whipped around like a mane, and his eyes burned red.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces arrived on his heels—First Rate martial artists and three Peak masters!
“Wipe out those Jin Family of Taiyuan bastards!”
“The Sect Leader is here! The Sect Leader has come!”
“Waaaah!”
The cheers rekindled their fading will to fight. Lee Cheonbaek surged down the path that had opened before him.
“Kill those treacherous Jin Family of Taiyuan bastards!”
Jin Wikyung was not about to stand by and watch.
“The time has come.”
The Head Elder answered.
“I agree.”
In truth, he had not welcomed Lee Cheonbaek’s arrival. A certain amount of attrition would have made the cleanup easier.
But neither the Jin Family of Taiyuan nor the Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered significant losses yet.
It doesn’t matter. They’ll be making their move anyway.
The two great powers claimed to rule Shanxi, but compared to them, they were insignificant.
Even at the height of its power, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been treated as nothing more than a martial family from the frontier. How could it possibly stand against them?
A mere martial family...
The Head Elder swallowed a bitter smile and drew his sword.
Shing.
For many years, he had carried two swords—one in his heart and one at his waist.
There was no need for further words.
“I’ll handle Lee Cheonbaek.”
“Please do.”

Who was Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek? The man who had founded the Mount Heng Sword Sect with nothing but a single sword, and who now meant to become the ruler of an entire city. Enemy or not, there was no denying he was a Peak martial artist of the highest caliber.
I want to fight him.
But Jin Wikyung forced down the heat in his blood.
This battle would decide the fate of his family. He had to set aside his fighting spirit.
“Wipeng.”
“Yes.”
Wipeng had already drawn his sharp, narrow sword and taken his place at Jin Wikyung’s side.
“You and I will handle the rest.”
“As you command.”
There was not a trace of hesitation in his answer. Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and drew his own sword—the treasured blade passed down through generations of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
It was the only thing left behind by the father who had vanished one day without a trace.
I’m going to travel around the Central Plains for a while. Use this in the meantime.
Remembering the letter stuffed carelessly into the scabbard made Jin Wikyung’s blood boil all over again.
Travel around the Central Plains, my ass. You spent your whole life having fun.
He had no idea where that so-called Family Head was or what he was doing, and his second brother, thousands of li away, had probably only just received the letter.
I have to protect them.
Martial artists, maids, servants, children.
Jin Wikyung was the Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan now. No one else.
Whether they lived or died was a burden he alone had to bear.
We will win.
Jin Wikyung’s eyes flared wide. He raised his sword and unleashed an azure dragon’s roar.
“Don’t let a single one of them live!”
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
The Jin Family’s masters kicked off the ground and soared into the air. At the signal, a single fire arrow rose high behind them.
That was when dozens of figures stood up along the cliffs.
“Fire!”
Beneath a sudden rain of arrows, the clash between the masters who would decide the course of the battle began.
Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek was a born martial artist.
Blessed with an innate talent for martial arts and the instincts of a beast, he had cut down his enemies and fulfilled his ambitions one after another.

He had founded the Mount Heng Sword Sect, then strengthened it by absorbing the surrounding factions one by one. His aim was to lay the foundation for a great family that would one day be recognized even in the Central Plains.
“Sect Leader! The Young Master...”
Then, one day, his second son came home a corpse.
He had not died in a fair duel. Deadly poison had killed him, blood pouring from all seven orifices.
Lee Cheonbaek swore an oath.
He would kill and burn everything connected to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
And now Jin Wikyung stood before him.
Flames blazed in Lee Cheonbaek’s eyes.
“You bastard—!”
He charged like a beast. His sword, imbued with one jiazi of internal energy, shone milky white.
With this much power, it could cut through any armor or divine weapon.
That bastard dies here!
Certain of his victory, Lee Cheonbaek was about to swing when—
“Oho. Sword Energy?”
A quiet voice came from behind him.
Lee Cheonbaek’s heart sank.
How?
He had given up his back far too easily. His response was lightning-fast. Gripping his sword in reverse, he stabbed behind him.
Whoosh.
The blade pierced empty air, but the attack bought him time. Only then did he get a look at his opponent.
A beard hung down to the man’s chest, and a relaxed smile played at the corners of his mouth.
He was a white-haired old man.
Lee Cheonbaek recognized him at once.
“Blade of Flowers?”
The Head Elder nodded.
“I haven’t heard that name in a long time. And you must be Lee Cheonbaek.”
“That’s right.”
Even as he answered, a chill ran down Lee Cheonbaek’s spine.
He did not dare look for Jin Wikyung or check how the battle was unfolding. If he took his eyes off the old man, he felt as though his head would come off at once.
Coincidence? No.
It was true that the sight of Jin Wikyung had driven him into a frenzy. It was also true that impatience had gotten the better of him.
But Lee Cheonbaek was a Peak master.
A Peak master who had reached the level of injuring others with Sword Energy.
There could only be one answer.
A master!
Whether by a full form or half a form, the old man before him stood above Lee Cheonbaek.
Lee Cheonbaek tightened his grip on his beloved sword.
“I’ve heard much of your reputation.”
“Reputation? I’m nothing more than an old man put out to pasture.”
“Then why didn’t you stay there?”
“You’re still young, so there’s a lot you don’t understand. The older you get, the more important it is to move around once in a while.”
Lee Cheonbaek ground his teeth at the Head Elder’s sly manner.
Damn old man.
He had been watching the Jin Family of Taiyuan for a long time.
He knew there was a faction centered around the Head Elder that opposed the Family Head. He had even privately hoped the family would split from within.
Instead, the exact opposite had happened.
So when an outside enemy invades, they unite as one?
Lee Cheonbaek stared at the Head Elder with heavy eyes, then opened his mouth.
“How strong are you?”
“As strong as you believe me to be.”
“Word games.”
“I was thirty when they called me Blade of Flowers.”
The Head Elder had already been a Peak martial artist at thirty.
Now he was seventy. How much had his martial arts changed since then?
After a moment’s thought, Lee Cheonbaek gave a wry laugh.
I’ve grown old too.
Blood Wolf Sword.
In his youth, Lee Cheonbaek had been unstoppable. Without an exceptional martial art or a respectable master, he had carved his way through everything on his own.
Even against an opponent a level above him, he never backed down. He charged like a wolf and tore out their throats.
I lived half my life that way...
At some point, people had started calling him Sect Leader instead of Blood Wolf Sword.
Blood relatives, subordinates, wealth.
The things he had to protect had piled up like a mountain.
He spent less time training and more time handling affairs. When the moment came to act, he stopped to think instead.
Just as he was doing now.
“Why are you laughing?”
Lee Cheonbaek answered the Head Elder’s question.
“I’m laughing because I find myself pathetic.”
“You’re afraid of me.”
Lee Cheonbaek nodded in silence.
“Were you afraid of death?”
“For a very brief moment.”
“And now?”
“I’m going to kill you.”
“Someone of your level can’t manage that.”
“You have to measure them to know which is longer, don’t you?”
“That’s what the short ones always say. They never realize that even after you measure, the result doesn’t change.”
“You have a sharp tongue.”
“My tongue isn’t the only thing that’s sharp.”
The Head Elder lowered his sword.
It looked like an ordinary blue-steel sword, but the moment it entered his hand, it began to give off a vicious killing edge.
“Come at me first.”
Lee Cheonbaek did not refuse.
His blade drew in one jiazi of internal energy, raising a shimmering haze of light.
The level of injuring others with Sword Energy—a realm countless martial artists dreamed of reaching.
Tssss.
The instant the Sword Energy rose three chi—about ten centimeters—Lee Cheonbaek shot forward.
A unique martial art, perfected through countless real battles, unfolded from his fingertips.
Whoosh! Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Boom!
Sword Energy slashed in every direction. Screams erupted amid the mounds of dirt blasted into the air.
“Graaagh!”
They were the cries of martial artists caught in the gap.
Every voice belonged to a young man.
A red warning light went on in Lee Cheonbaek’s mind.
Behind!
He spun and swung in the same motion.
He saw a white beard fluttering in the wind.
And the sword in the old man’s hand.
Boom!
Kh.
The thunderous impact sent Lee Cheonbaek reeling backward. He was not even given time to feel the pain in his wrist.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Every time the two swords met, thunder and lightning rolled.
Sword Energy streamed from their blades, smashing the ground and tearing through the air.
Whoosh!
“What in the world is that...?”
The martial artists on both sides forgot their own battles. They could only stare, dumbstruck, at the incredible life-and-death duel.
At that moment, every one of them was thinking the same thing.
Are those two really human beings like us?
The ceaseless thunder. A display of Sword Energy so dazzling that merely watching it left them spellbound.
The movements of the two men at its center were faster and stronger than anyone they had ever seen.
Someone murmured as if groaning.
“So this is a Peak master...”
To their eyes, either man could have won.
But the superiority in strength was obvious.
After some three hundred exchanges, the Head Elder’s swordplay changed.
Whoosh—slice!
“Ghk.”
Lee Cheonbaek bit down on his lip.
Blood streamed from the forearm the Head Elder’s sword had raked.
The strength drained from his sword hand.
Of all things.
He immediately shifted the sword to his other hand, but he was right-handed by nature.
Even fighting at full strength might not have been enough. Now that his sword arm was injured, the outcome was all but decided.
Boom!
Crack.
A single blow snapped his wrist.
His Sword Energy, weakened by the severe drain on his internal energy, could no longer stand against the Head Elder.
But Lee Cheonbaek did not give up.
Not yet. It isn’t over yet.
He had taken worse injuries than this, plenty of times.
Drawing on the strength in his arm, waist, and legs, Lee Cheonbaek swung his sword.
No—he tried to.
Slash!
This time, it was the knee.
The severed tendons gave way, and Lee Cheonbaek’s knee buckled against his will.
His sword carved uselessly through empty air.
Shhk. Shhk-shhk-shhk.
His side. His shoulder. His chest.
Lightning stabbed and sliced through his entire body. The fierce Sword Energy did more than cut flesh and bone—it churned his insides.
“Bleeegh!”
Lee Cheonbaek vomited blood mixed with pieces of his organs and looked up at the Head Elder through clouded eyes.
The old man’s face was impassive.
There was no thrill at having defeated his opponent, nor any joy at the war’s end.
To him, this was nothing more than the natural outcome.
“Cough... So Shanxi’s Number One was standing right in front of me.”
“If you’re not Number One Under Heaven, you’re nothing more than a martial brute from the frontier. Neither you nor I are made for such heights.”
“Tell me what you want. I’ll give you my neck. I’ll make my men surrender, and I’ll seal the sect for ten years—or a hundred. So...”
“No. What I want is annihilation. Complete annihilation, without a single blade of grass left standing.”
“Don’t ask me that. If you had won, it would have been our family facing annihilation.”
Lee Cheonbaek glared at the Head Elder with bloodshot eyes.
He wanted to snap that wrinkled neck then and there.
But grievously wounded as he was, all he could do was force out his voice.
“Jin Family of Taiyuan. You started this, didn’t you? You killed that boy—my son!”
“Ah, Lee Seogeun. Yes. That child was where it all began.”
A sardonic smile touched the Head Elder’s lips.
Even the master of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, one of the two powers that divided Shanxi between them, had failed to notice their intervention.
Even now, with death staring him in the face.
When you meet Yama, ask him who killed Lee Seogeun.
The Sound Transmission burrowed into Lee Cheonbaek’s ear, and his eyes flared wide.
“What does that mean...?”
It was a thoroughly impulsive act.
Perhaps pity for Lee Cheonbaek, who was about to die knowing nothing.
Or perhaps it was nothing more than an old man’s whim.
Consider it fare for the road to the afterlife. Think it over on your long journey.
The Head Elder raised his sword.
The light of the setting sun beyond the winter ridge splintered across the blade.
With this...
With the death of the giant called Lee Cheonbaek, the Mount Heng Sword Sect would collapse.
Those who resisted would die. Those who surrendered would be taken prisoner.
One war would end...
And a new war would begin the moment everyone was drunk on victory.
It’s over.
At last, the Head Elder’s sword moved.
Screeeech—!
A sharp sound tore through the air.
Sensing his end, Lee Cheonbaek closed his eyes.
The blade, wrapped in blue Sword Energy, traced a beautiful arc.
Slice.
But both the sound that had come first and the direction of the sword were not what Lee Cheonbaek had expected.
A spear had come flying at the Head Elder’s back out of nowhere, and he split it apart with Sword Energy.
The old man roared in fury.
“Who the hell are you?”
The answer came an instant later.
“It’s me, you fucking bastard!”
The Head Elder saw the face of a young man standing tall on a low hill, and groaned.
“Jin Taekyung?”

“You bastards!”
Lee Cheonbaek appeared with a thunderous roar.
His half-gray hair whipped around like a mane, and his eyes burned red.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces arrived on his heels—First Rate martial artists and three Peak masters!
“Wipe out those Jin Family of Taiyuan bastards!”
“The Sect Leader is here!
The Sect Leader has come!”
“Waaaah!”
The cheers rekindled their fading will to fight.
Lee Cheonbaek surged down the path that had opened before him.
“Kill those treacherous Jin Family of Taiyuan bastards!”
Jin Wikyung was not about to stand by and watch.
“The time has come.”
The Head Elder answered.
“I agree.”
In truth, he had not welcomed Lee Cheonbaek’s arrival.
A certain amount of attrition would have made the cleanup easier.
But neither the Jin Family of Taiyuan nor the Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered significant losses yet.
It doesn’t matter.
They’ll be making their move anyway.
The two great powers claimed to rule Shanxi, but compared to them, they were insignificant.
Even at the height of its power, the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been treated as nothing more than a martial family from the frontier.
How could it possibly stand against them?
A mere martial family...
The Head Elder swallowed a bitter smile and drew his sword.
Shing.
For many years, he had carried two swords—one in his heart and one at his waist.
There was no need for further words.
“I’ll handle Lee Cheonbaek.”
“Please do.”
Who was Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek?
The man who had founded the Mount Heng Sword Sect with nothing but a single sword, and who now meant to become the ruler of an entire city.
Enemy or not, there was no denying he was a Peak martial artist of the highest caliber.
I want to fight him.
But Jin Wikyung forced down the heat in his blood.
This battle would decide the fate of his family.
He had to set aside his fighting spirit.
“Wipeng.”
“Yes.”
Wipeng had already drawn his sharp, narrow sword and taken his place at Jin Wikyung’s side.
“You and I will handle the rest.”
“As you command.”
There was not a trace of hesitation in his answer.
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and drew his own sword—the treasured blade passed down through generations of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
It was the only thing left behind by the father who had vanished one day without a trace.
I’m going to travel around the Central Plains for a while.
Use this in the meantime.
Remembering the letter stuffed carelessly into the scabbard made Jin Wikyung’s blood boil all over again.
Travel around the Central Plains, my ass.
You spent your whole life having fun.
He had no idea where that so-called Family Head was or what he was doing, and his second brother, thousands of li away, had probably only just received the letter.
I have to protect them.
Martial artists, maids, servants, children.
Jin Wikyung was the Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan now.
No one else.
Whether they lived or died was a burden he alone had to bear.
We will win.
Jin Wikyung’s eyes flared wide.
He raised his sword and unleashed an azure dragon’s roar.
“Don’t let a single one of them live!”
Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!
The Jin Family’s masters kicked off the ground and soared into the air.
At the signal, a single fire arrow rose high behind them.
That was when dozens of figures stood up along the cliffs.
“Fire!”
Beneath a sudden rain of arrows, the clash between the masters who would decide the course of the battle began.
Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek was a born martial artist.
Blessed with an innate talent for martial arts and the instincts of a beast, he had cut down his enemies and fulfilled his ambitions one after another.
He had founded the Mount Heng Sword Sect, then strengthened it by absorbing the surrounding factions one by one.
His aim was to lay the foundation for a great family that would one day be recognized even in the Central Plains.
“Sect Leader!
The Young Master...”
Then, one day, his second son came home a corpse.
He had not died in a fair duel.
Deadly poison had killed him, blood pouring from all seven orifices.
Lee Cheonbaek swore an oath.
He would kill and burn everything connected to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
And now Jin Wikyung stood before him.
Flames blazed in Lee Cheonbaek’s eyes.
“You bastard—!”
He charged like a beast.
His sword, imbued with one jiazi of internal energy, shone milky white.
With this much power, it could cut through any armor or divine weapon.
That bastard dies here!
Certain of his victory, Lee Cheonbaek was about to swing when—
“Oho.
Sword Energy?”
A quiet voice came from behind him.
Lee Cheonbaek’s heart sank.
How?
He had given up his back far too easily.
His response was lightning-fast.
Gripping his sword in reverse, he stabbed behind him.
Whoosh.
The blade pierced empty air, but the attack bought him time.
Only then did he get a look at his opponent.
A beard hung down to the man’s chest, and a relaxed smile played at the corners of his mouth.
He was a white-haired old man.
Lee Cheonbaek recognized him at once.
“Blade of Flowers?”
The Head Elder nodded.
“I haven’t heard that name in a long time.
And you must be Lee Cheonbaek.”
“That’s right.”
Even as he answered, a chill ran down Lee Cheonbaek’s spine.
He did not dare look for Jin Wikyung or check how the battle was unfolding.
If he took his eyes off the old man, he felt as though his head would come off at once.
Coincidence?
No.
It was true that the sight of Jin Wikyung had driven him into a frenzy.
It was also true that impatience had gotten the better of him.
But Lee Cheonbaek was a Peak master.
A Peak master who had reached the level of injuring others with Sword Energy.
There could only be one answer.
A master!
Whether by a full form or half a form, the old man before him stood above Lee Cheonbaek.
Lee Cheonbaek tightened his grip on his beloved sword.
“I’ve heard much of your reputation.”
“Reputation?
I’m nothing more than an old man put out to pasture.”
“Then why didn’t you stay there?”
“You’re still young, so there’s a lot you don’t understand.
The older you get, the more important it is to move around once in a while.”
Lee Cheonbaek ground his teeth at the Head Elder’s sly manner.
Damn old man.
He had been watching the Jin Family of Taiyuan for a long time.
He knew there was a faction centered around the Head Elder that opposed the Family Head.
He had even privately hoped the family would split from within.
Instead, the exact opposite had happened.
So when an outside enemy invades, they unite as one?
Lee Cheonbaek stared at the Head Elder with heavy eyes, then opened his mouth.
“How strong are you?”
“As strong as you believe me to be.”
“Word games.”
“I was thirty when they called me Blade of Flowers.”
The Head Elder had already been a Peak martial artist at thirty.
Now he was seventy.
How much had his martial arts changed since then?
After a moment’s thought, Lee Cheonbaek gave a wry laugh.
I’ve grown old too.
Blood Wolf Sword.
In his youth, Lee Cheonbaek had been unstoppable.
Without an exceptional martial art or a respectable master, he had carved his way through everything on his own.
Even against an opponent a level above him, he never backed down.
He charged like a wolf and tore out their throats.
I lived half my life that way...
At some point, people had started calling him Sect Leader instead of Blood Wolf Sword.
Blood relatives, subordinates, wealth.
The things he had to protect had piled up like a mountain.
He spent less time training and more time handling affairs.
When the moment came to act, he stopped to think instead.
Just as he was doing now.
“Why are you laughing?”
Lee Cheonbaek answered the Head Elder’s question.
“I’m laughing because I find myself pathetic.”
“You’re afraid of me.”
Lee Cheonbaek nodded in silence.
“Were you afraid of death?”
“For a very brief moment.”
“And now?”
“I’m going to kill you.”
“Someone of your level can’t manage that.”
“You have to measure them to know which is longer, don’t you?”
“That’s what the short ones always say.
They never realize that even after you measure, the result doesn’t change.”
“You have a sharp tongue.”
“My tongue isn’t the only thing that’s sharp.”
The Head Elder lowered his sword.
It looked like an ordinary blue-steel sword, but the moment it entered his hand, it began to give off a vicious killing edge.
“Come at me first.”
Lee Cheonbaek did not refuse.
His blade drew in one jiazi of internal energy, raising a shimmering haze of light.
The level of injuring others with Sword Energy—a realm countless martial artists dreamed of reaching.
Tssss.
The instant the Sword Energy rose three chi—about ten centimeters—Lee Cheonbaek shot forward.
A unique martial art, perfected through countless real battles, unfolded from his fingertips.
Whoosh!
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Boom!
Sword Energy slashed in every direction.
Screams erupted amid the mounds of dirt blasted into the air.
“Graaagh!”
They were the cries of martial artists caught in the gap.
Every voice belonged to a young man.
A red warning light went on in Lee Cheonbaek’s mind.
Behind!
He spun and swung in the same motion.
He saw a white beard fluttering in the wind.
And the sword in the old man’s hand.
Boom!
Kh.
The thunderous impact sent Lee Cheonbaek reeling backward.
He was not even given time to feel the pain in his wrist.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Every time the two swords met, thunder and lightning rolled.
Sword Energy streamed from their blades, smashing the ground and tearing through the air.
Whoosh!
“What in the world is that...?”
The martial artists on both sides forgot their own battles.
They could only stare, dumbstruck, at the incredible life-and-death duel.
At that moment, every one of them was thinking the same thing.
Are those two really human beings like us?
The ceaseless thunder.
A display of Sword Energy so dazzling that merely watching it left them spellbound.
The movements of the two men at its center were faster and stronger than anyone they had ever seen.
Someone murmured as if groaning.
“So this is a Peak master...”
To their eyes, either man could have won.
But the superiority in strength was obvious.
After some three hundred exchanges, the Head Elder’s swordplay changed.
Whoosh—slice!
“Ghk.”
Lee Cheonbaek bit down on his lip.
Blood streamed from the forearm the Head Elder’s sword had raked.
The strength drained from his sword hand.
Of all things.
He immediately shifted the sword to his other hand, but he was right-handed by nature.
Even fighting at full strength might not have been enough.
Now that his sword arm was injured, the outcome was all but decided.
Boom!
Crack.
A single blow snapped his wrist.
His Sword Energy, weakened by the severe drain on his internal energy, could no longer stand against the Head Elder.
But Lee Cheonbaek did not give up.
Not yet.
It isn’t over yet.
He had taken worse injuries than this, plenty of times.
Drawing on the strength in his arm, waist, and legs, Lee Cheonbaek swung his sword.
No—he tried to.
Slash!
This time, it was the knee.
The severed tendons gave way, and Lee Cheonbaek’s knee buckled against his will.
His sword carved uselessly through empty air.
Shhk.
Shhk-shhk-shhk.
His side.
His shoulder.
His chest.
Lightning stabbed and sliced through his entire body.
The fierce Sword Energy did more than cut flesh and bone—it churned his insides.
“Bleeegh!”
Lee Cheonbaek vomited blood mixed with pieces of his organs and looked up at the Head Elder through clouded eyes.
The old man’s face was impassive.
There was no thrill at having defeated his opponent, nor any joy at the war’s end.
To him, this was nothing more than the natural outcome.
“Cough...
So Shanxi’s Number One was standing right in front of me.”
“If you’re not Number One Under Heaven, you’re nothing more than a martial brute from the frontier.
Neither you nor I are made for such heights.”
“Tell me what you want.
I’ll give you my neck.
I’ll make my men surrender, and I’ll seal the sect for ten years—or a hundred.
“No.
What I want is annihilation.
Complete annihilation, without a single blade of grass left standing.”
“Don’t ask me that.
If you had won, it would have been our family facing annihilation.”
Lee Cheonbaek glared at the Head Elder with bloodshot eyes.
He wanted to snap that wrinkled neck then and there.
But grievously wounded as he was, all he could do was force out his voice.
“Jin Family of Taiyuan.
You started this, didn’t you?
You killed that boy—my son!”
“Ah, Lee Seogeun.
Yes.
That child was where it all began.”
A sardonic smile touched the Head Elder’s lips.
Even the master of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, one of the two powers that divided Shanxi between them, had failed to notice their intervention.
Even now, with death staring him in the face.
When you meet Yama, ask him who killed Lee Seogeun.
The Sound Transmission burrowed into Lee Cheonbaek’s ear, and his eyes flared wide.
“What does that mean...?”
It was a thoroughly impulsive act.
Perhaps pity for Lee Cheonbaek, who was about to die knowing nothing.
Or perhaps it was nothing more than an old man’s whim.
Consider it fare for the road to the afterlife.
Think it over on your long journey.
The Head Elder raised his sword.
The light of the setting sun beyond the winter ridge splintered across the blade.
With this...
With the death of the giant called Lee Cheonbaek, the Mount Heng Sword Sect would collapse.
Those who resisted would die.
Those who surrendered would be taken prisoner.
One war would end...
And a new war would begin the moment everyone was drunk on victory.
It’s over.
At last, the Head Elder’s sword moved.
Screeeech—!
A sharp sound tore through the air.
Sensing his end, Lee Cheonbaek closed his eyes.
The blade, wrapped in blue Sword Energy, traced a beautiful arc.
Slice.
But both the sound that had come first and the direction of the sword were not what Lee Cheonbaek had expected.
A spear had come flying at the Head Elder’s back out of nowhere, and he split it apart with Sword Energy.
The old man roared in fury.
“Who the hell are you?”
The answer came an instant later.
“It’s me, you fucking bastard!”
The Head Elder saw the face of a young man standing tall on a low hill, and groaned.
“Jin Taekyung?”

chapters.title: Chapter 57
paragraphs: “Faster! Go faster!”
“Huff... huff!”
We ran like mad. Hyuk Mujin was panting like he was about to drop dead, but he didn’t. Whenever he started to slow down, I pressed the spearhead against his back, and he took off like Red Hare.
Then the sounds began to reach us.
Screams. Steel clashing against steel...
Good. The battle wasn’t over yet.
Relief hit me, and my heart hammered at the same time. The fighting was still going on, but I still hadn’t confirmed whether Jin Wikyung was alive or dead.
What if he died because we were a minute—or even a second—too late?
If that happens...
Crack.
My grip tightened around the spear before I realized it. I drew internal energy from my dantian and sent it flowing into both legs.
“C-Captain!”
I kept running, leaving the reconnaissance squad’s voices fading behind me. The countless tracks left by the main force and the growing din of the battlefield showed me the way.
Stay alive. Stay alive. Please, stay—
There!
Below a low hill, less than two hundred meters away, countless martial artists were locked in a bloody struggle, killing and being killed.
“Die!”
“Gaaah!”
Corpses and blood—and more corpses, more blood!
The sight before me was so brutal that it left me speechless.
If my years as a Hunter hadn’t hardened me to this sort of thing, I probably would have stood there stunned for a long time.
Jin Wikyung! Where is Jin Wikyung?
But someone else caught my eye first.
White hair, unmistakable even from this distance.
The Head Elder!
He stood in front of someone, sword in hand.
The Head Elder’s back blocked most of my view, but the man kneeling in front of him was huge and held a sword of his own.
A big man with a sword?
Only one person came to mind.
Jin Wikyung. If I wanted to save him, I had to act now.
Open Inventory.
My Murim Inventory was packed with all kinds of things.
The spear I pulled out was one of them, with a wooden shaft and a steel head.
Equip Weapon.
Spear in hand, I took several steps back.
Two hundred meters. An impossibly long distance—especially if I was trying to hit someone with a thrown spear.
But I had to do it.
No reason I can’t.
Strength, Stamina, Agility.
I pushed the stats I’d built up traveling between Murim and reality to their limits.
With internal energy in my arm, I could send the spear farther and harder.
“Hup.”
I held my breath and stepped forward. The first step was slow, the final step heavy. My arm snapped out like a whip, and the spear shot from my fingertips.
Fwoooosh!
The throw was faster and more accurate than I’d expected. It looked ready to punch straight through the Head Elder’s back.
But then...
Shhk.
What the hell was that?
Blue light flashed, and the spear split cleanly in two from the tip of the spearhead to the end of the shaft.
I couldn’t tell whether I’d thrown a spear or a birthday cake.
“Who the hell are you?”
The old man had quite a set of lungs.
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”
That was probably the first time in the Head Elder’s life anyone had cursed him like that.
To make matters worse, he and I belonged to the same family in Murim. Going by the family tree, the difference in seniority between us was roughly that of an archaeopteryx and a chick.
That alone was plenty of reason for him to be stunned, but I still had one finishing blow left.
“The Head Elder is—!”
My voice, loaded with internal energy, thundered across the battlefield. Even I was startled by how loud it was. I could only imagine what it sounded like to everyone else.
I stared at his cold, frozen face in the distance and shouted with all my might.
“A traitor!”
Jin Wikyung heard the voice immediately after bringing down all three Peak masters of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
No, it wasn’t just him. Everyone on the battlefield heard the shout.
“Who the hell are you?”
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”
Cursing?
That was common enough on a battlefield. But it was a different matter when the target was the Head Elder and the young man who had appeared out of nowhere to hurl such abuse at him was Jin Taekyung.
“Isn’t that... isn’t that the Third Young Master?”
“What? That’s Jin Taekyung? But why?”
“What’s going on?”
Jin Wikyung was wondering the same thing.
What in the world is happening?

His youngest brother, who should have been in the rear, had appeared on the battlefield. That alone was bewildering enough, but now he was hurling unspeakable abuse at one of the family’s most senior elders.
Wipeng, standing beside him, muttered, “He’s completely lost his mind.”
Jin Wikyung was about to nod without thinking when—
“The Head Elder is—!”
An even bigger bomb dropped.
“A traitor!”
An icy silence fell over the battlefield. Even the sporadic clash of weapons came to an abrupt stop.
Everyone stared blankly at Jin Taekyung.
What kind of bullshit is this?
Betrayal? The Head Elder?
Is he drunk? The Third Young Master must be slipping back into his old habits.
The martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan naturally thought so, and those of the Mount Heng Sword Sect were no different.
Even the senior members who had recently begun to think better of Jin Taekyung gaped at him.
“What a lunatic.”
“Does he have any idea who the Old Master is?”
If anyone deserved the most credit for this war, it was undoubtedly the Head Elder.
He had helped Jin Wikyung unite the family’s forces, and in today’s battle, he had defeated Lee Cheonbaek.
Even setting aside his contributions to the war, Jin Taekyung’s claim could only sound absurd.
Who was the Head Elder?

He was a master of the previous generation whose title, the Blade of Flowers, was renowned even across the Central Plains. He was a symbol of righteousness who had struck down countless fiends during the Great Faction War.
Every martial artist in Shanxi held some measure of respect for him.
“That man? A son of a bitch? A traitor?”
“Good heavens. That boy is smearing shit over the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s three-hundred-year history.”
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect—everyone present seemed to share the same thought.
With at least one exception.
The Head Elder. Betrayal.
The moment Jin Wikyung heard his youngest brother’s words, he felt all the blood in his body run cold.
The vague sense that something was wrong had finally taken shape.
Lee Seogeun’s death was where it began.
He had died after being poisoned with a lethal toxin. The Mount Heng Sword Sect had named the Jin Family of Taiyuan as the culprit, sparking the war.
But the most important question had been left unanswered.
Who was the killer?
Even now, with the war nearing its end, the culprit hiding behind it all had never been identified. No—precisely because the war was nearing its end, no one cared about the killer’s identity anymore.
Survival of the fittest. The strong would survive and claim everything.
This war... was wrong from the very beginning.
Lee Seogeun’s death.
The unnaturally rapid spread of the rumors.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had declared war, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had responded. That was how the fighting had begun in earnest.
And the Head Elder was there.
The Head Elder, who had shut himself away from the world, had emerged immediately after news of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning reached the family. His role within the family had been enormous.
A respected martial artist. A revered elder of the family.
Without the Head Elder’s active support, the Jin Family of Taiyuan might have split in two.
We made it this far because of his help.
Then Jin Wikyung turned the thought around.
We made it this far because this was exactly what the Head Elder wanted.
In a moment too brief to even call an instant, Jin Wikyung reached his conclusion and spoke.
“Wipeng.”
“Your orders.”
“Cut down the First Elder.”
“What?”
The stooped, emaciated old man—the First Elder—stared wide-eyed.
The senior members nearby were equally shocked.
“L-Lesser Family Head!”
“What is the meaning of this...?”
But Wipeng did not hesitate. Before anyone could react, his sword was already flying toward the First Elder’s chest.
Clang-clang-clang!
Two swords suddenly cut in and knocked Wipeng’s blade aside.
Their wielders were two enormously tall, fat old men.
They were the Second and Third Elders, who, together with the First Elder, called themselves the Head Elder’s hands and feet.
Wipeng’s brow twitched when he saw the faint Sword Energy clinging to their blades.
“You were hiding your martial arts.”
The First Elder answered with a punch.
Boom!
The profound internal energy he had accumulated over his long life sent Wipeng flying. Then the First Elder straightened his stooped back.
The entire field froze at the emergence of yet another Peak master, one who had spent his life hidden in the Head Elder’s shadow.
“First Elder, what... what is this?”
“Then could it be...?”
Betrayal.
The word stamped itself into everyone’s mind.
“That’s impossible!”
The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a shrill shout. If the Elders were the Head Elder’s hands and feet, then he had served faithfully as the First Elder’s.
“Elder, Lesser Family Head. There seems to have been some misunderstanding...”
But he never finished.
The First Elder jerked his chin, and the Second Elder moved with blinding speed, severing the White Tiger Hall Leader’s neck.
Shhk. Thud.
Jin Wikyung and the First Elder locked eyes across the space between them.
“You recruited the White Tiger Hall Leader too?”
“He was loud. That was all. The others were no different.”
Jin Wikyung’s guess had been half right and half wrong.
The Elders had betrayed them, but the senior members of the Elders’ faction had not.
“Then why... Ah!”
“Sharp. I’ll give you that.”
The First Elder drew a dark, grimy bamboo tube from inside his robes. The fuse was already burning, and almost nothing remained.

“How could we share such an important secret with men like them? Their job was done once they’d thrown the family into confusion. It made things easier if they had no idea what was happening outside.”
Jin Wikyung screamed, “Stop him!”
“You’re too late.”
The First Elder was right.
The moment the fuse burned to its end, something burst, and a red flame shot high into the sky.
Fwish—boom!
It was a signal.

The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi changed in an instant—the Samdo Sect, an alliance of three sects; the saber-focused Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been raining arrows down from the cliffs without pause.
“Kill everyone in your path!”
“No exceptions! Wipe them all out!”
They were no longer the clumsy Third Rate martial artists they had seemed to be. Killing intent flowed from their eyes, and their sword paths were sharp.
This wasn’t something they prepared overnight.
Jin Wikyung’s expression hardened.
Boom!
The Head Elder looked up at the sky. Before the red flame had even faded, thunderous shouts erupted from every direction.
Too fast. Far too fast.

The signal was supposed to be sent only after the Mount Heng Sword Sect had been annihilated. The Five Gates of Shanxi were a blade honed over decades. It had to be swung once and bring everything to a lightning-fast end.
All things have their proper flow.
The plan that had proceeded without a hitch was beginning to unravel.
As the Head Elder smiled bitterly, a voice reached his ears.
“So... it was you.”
Lee Cheonbaek.
His voice was faint, but his eyes burned more fiercely than ever.
“You still have the strength to speak?”
“I’ll tear you apart while you’re still alive.”

No sooner had Lee Cheonbaek finished speaking than blood gushed from his mouth. The Head Elder pressed one of his acupoints and murmured, “That would be inconvenient just yet. You still have something to do.”
Lee Cheonbaek despaired.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered heavy losses, but several hundred martial artists still remained. With its entire leadership destroyed, if the Sect Leader were now taken prisoner...
Kill me instead!
The anguished cry never left his mouth. The Head Elder pressed the Mute Acupoint, taking his voice. Then his hand brushed the Paralysis Acupoint, and Lee Cheonbaek’s body went rigid.
He had become a living corpse with his eyes still open.
“You bastard! Get your hands off him!”
At the same moment, something shrieked through the air.
Fwoooosh!
The Head Elder did not panic. He swept his sword upward from below. Beyond the spear splitting in two along the line of his Sword Energy, Jin Taekyung was charging toward him at terrifying speed.
“Aaaaaah!”
“Captain! Please slow down a little!”
And with him came a dozen or so riffraff who had appeared from who knew where.
