The throw was faster and more accurate than I’d expected.
It looked ready to punch straight through the Head Elder’s back.
But then...
Shhk.
What the hell was that?
Blue light flashed, and the spear split cleanly in two from the tip of the spearhead to the end of the shaft.
I couldn’t tell whether I’d thrown a spear or a birthday cake.
“Who the hell are you?”
The old man had quite a set of lungs.
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”
That was probably the first time in the Head Elder’s life anyone had cursed him like that.
To make matters worse, he and I belonged to the same family in Murim.
Going by the family tree, the difference in seniority between us was roughly that of an archaeopteryx and a chick.
That alone was plenty of reason for him to be stunned, but I still had one finishing blow left.
“The Head Elder is—!”
My voice, loaded with internal energy, thundered across the battlefield.
Even I was startled by how loud it was.
I could only imagine what it sounded like to everyone else.
I stared at his cold, frozen face in the distance and shouted with all my might.
“A traitor!”
Jin Wikyung heard the voice immediately after bringing down all three Peak masters of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
No, it wasn’t just him.
Everyone on the battlefield heard the shout.
“Who the hell are you?”
“It’s me, you son of a bitch!”
Cursing?
That was common enough on a battlefield.
But it was a different matter when the target was the Head Elder and the young man who had appeared out of nowhere to hurl such abuse at him was Jin Taekyung.
“Isn’t that... isn’t that the Third Young Master?”
“What?
That’s Jin Taekyung?
But why?”
“What’s going on?”
Jin Wikyung was wondering the same thing.
What in the world is happening?
His youngest brother, who should have been in the rear, had appeared on the battlefield.
That alone was bewildering enough, but now he was hurling unspeakable abuse at one of the family’s most senior elders.
Wipeng, standing beside him, muttered, “He’s completely lost his mind.”
Jin Wikyung was about to nod without thinking when—
“The Head Elder is—!”
An even bigger bomb dropped.
“A traitor!”
An icy silence fell over the battlefield.
Even the sporadic clash of weapons came to an abrupt stop.
Everyone stared blankly at Jin Taekyung.
What kind of bullshit is this?
Betrayal?
The Head Elder?
Is he drunk?
The Third Young Master must be slipping back into his old habits.
The martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan naturally thought so, and those of the Mount Heng Sword Sect were no different.
Even the senior members who had recently begun to think better of Jin Taekyung gaped at him.
“What a lunatic.”
“Does he have any idea who the Old Master is?”
If anyone deserved the most credit for this war, it was undoubtedly the Head Elder.
He had helped Jin Wikyung unite the family’s forces, and in today’s battle, he had defeated Lee Cheonbaek.
Even setting aside his contributions to the war, Jin Taekyung’s claim could only sound absurd.
Who was the Head Elder?
He was a master of the previous generation whose title, the Blade of Flowers, was renowned even across the Central Plains.
He was a symbol of righteousness who had struck down countless fiends during the Great Faction War.
Every martial artist in Shanxi held some measure of respect for him.
“That man?
A son of a bitch?
A traitor?”
“Good heavens.
That boy is smearing shit over the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s three-hundred-year history.”
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect—everyone present seemed to share the same thought.
With at least one exception.
The Head Elder.
Betrayal.
The moment Jin Wikyung heard his youngest brother’s words, he felt all the blood in his body run cold.
The vague sense that something was wrong had finally taken shape.
Lee Seogeun’s death was where it began.
He had died after being poisoned with a lethal toxin.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had named the Jin Family of Taiyuan as the culprit, sparking the war.
But the most important question had been left unanswered.
Who was the killer?
Even now, with the war nearing its end, the culprit hiding behind it all had never been identified.
No—precisely because the war was nearing its end, no one cared about the killer’s identity anymore.
Survival of the fittest.
The strong would survive and claim everything.
This war... was wrong from the very beginning.
Lee Seogeun’s death.
The unnaturally rapid spread of the rumors.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had declared war, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had responded.
That was how the fighting had begun in earnest.
And the Head Elder was there.
The Head Elder, who had shut himself away from the world, had emerged immediately after news of Lee Seogeun’s poisoning reached the family.
His role within the family had been enormous.
A respected martial artist.
A revered elder of the family.
Without the Head Elder’s active support, the Jin Family of Taiyuan might have split in two.
We made it this far because of his help.
Then Jin Wikyung turned the thought around.
We made it this far because this was exactly what the Head Elder wanted.
In a moment too brief to even call an instant, Jin Wikyung reached his conclusion and spoke.
“Wipeng.”
“Your orders.”
“Cut down the First Elder.”
“What?”
The stooped, emaciated old man—the First Elder—stared wide-eyed.
The senior members nearby were equally shocked.
“L-Lesser Family Head!”
“What is the meaning of this...?”
But Wipeng did not hesitate.
Before anyone could react, his sword was already flying toward the First Elder’s chest.
Clang-clang-clang!
Two swords suddenly cut in and knocked Wipeng’s blade aside.
Their wielders were two enormously tall, fat old men.
They were the Second and Third Elders, who, together with the First Elder, called themselves the Head Elder’s hands and feet.
Wipeng’s brow twitched when he saw the faint Sword Energy clinging to their blades.
“You were hiding your martial arts.”
The First Elder answered with a punch.
Boom!
The profound internal energy he had accumulated over his long life sent Wipeng flying.
Then the First Elder straightened his stooped back.
The entire field froze at the emergence of yet another Peak master, one who had spent his life hidden in the Head Elder’s shadow.
“First Elder, what... what is this?”
“Then could it be...?”
Betrayal.
The word stamped itself into everyone’s mind.
“That’s impossible!”
The White Tiger Hall Leader let out a shrill shout.
If the Elders were the Head Elder’s hands and feet, then he had served faithfully as the First Elder’s.
“Elder, Lesser Family Head.
There seems to have been some misunderstanding...”
But he never finished.
The First Elder jerked his chin, and the Second Elder moved with blinding speed, severing the White Tiger Hall Leader’s neck.
Shhk.
Thud.
Jin Wikyung and the First Elder locked eyes across the space between them.
“You recruited the White Tiger Hall Leader too?”
“He was loud.
That was all.
The others were no different.”
Jin Wikyung’s guess had been half right and half wrong.
The Elders had betrayed them, but the senior members of the Elders’ faction had not.
“Then why...
Ah!”
“Sharp.
I’ll give you that.”
The First Elder drew a dark, grimy bamboo tube from inside his robes.
The fuse was already burning, and almost nothing remained.
“How could we share such an important secret with men like them?
Their job was done once they’d thrown the family into confusion.
It made things easier if they had no idea what was happening outside.”
Jin Wikyung screamed, “Stop him!”
“You’re too late.”
The First Elder was right.
The moment the fuse burned to its end, something burst, and a red flame shot high into the sky.
Fwish—boom!
It was a signal.

The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects collectively known as the Five Gates of Shanxi changed in an instant—the Samdo Sect, an alliance of three sects; the saber-focused Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been raining arrows down from the cliffs without pause.
“Kill everyone in your path!”
“No exceptions!
Wipe them all out!”
They were no longer the clumsy Third Rate martial artists they had seemed to be.
Killing intent flowed from their eyes, and their sword paths were sharp.
This wasn’t something they prepared overnight.
Jin Wikyung’s expression hardened.
Boom!
The Head Elder looked up at the sky.
Before the red flame had even faded, thunderous shouts erupted from every direction.
Too fast.
Far too fast.
The signal was supposed to be sent only after the Mount Heng Sword Sect had been annihilated.
The Five Gates of Shanxi were a blade honed over decades.
It had to be swung once and bring everything to a lightning-fast end.
All things have their proper flow.
The plan that had proceeded without a hitch was beginning to unravel.
As the Head Elder smiled bitterly, a voice reached his ears.
“So... it was you.”
Lee Cheonbaek.
His voice was faint, but his eyes burned more fiercely than ever.
“You still have the strength to speak?”
“I’ll tear you apart while you’re still alive.”
No sooner had Lee Cheonbaek finished speaking than blood gushed from his mouth.
The Head Elder pressed one of his acupoints and murmured, “That would be inconvenient just yet.
You still have something to do.”
Lee Cheonbaek despaired.
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had suffered heavy losses, but several hundred martial artists still remained.
With its entire leadership destroyed, if the Sect Leader were now taken prisoner...
Kill me instead!
The anguished cry never left his mouth.
The Head Elder pressed the Mute Acupoint, taking his voice.
Then his hand brushed the Paralysis Acupoint, and Lee Cheonbaek’s body went rigid.
He had become a living corpse with his eyes still open.
“You bastard!
Get your hands off him!”
At the same moment, something shrieked through the air.
Fwoooosh!
The Head Elder did not panic.
He swept his sword upward from below.
Beyond the spear splitting in two along the line of his Sword Energy, Jin Taekyung was charging toward him at terrifying speed.
“Aaaaaah!”
“Captain!
Please slow down a little!”
And with him came a dozen or so riffraff who had appeared from who knew where.

chapters.title: Chapter 58
paragraphs: The battlefield descended into chaos. At the signal, two hundred martial artists suddenly turned and swarmed in every direction like a pack of wolves.
“Kill them all!”
“Aaaaargh!”
They weren’t quite on the level of Gwak Jun and the assassins we’d fought earlier, but they radiated an aura like well-honed blades.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect. If the martial artists of both factions joined forces, we’d have a real chance—but right now, that looked difficult.
This is bad.
Worst case, I might have to pull Jin Wikyung out and run.
I was thinking that when the reconnaissance squad arrived behind me, breathing hard.
“Captain, maybe we can—huff!”
The moment they saw what was happening in front of them, their eyes nearly popped out. Hyuk Mujin, who came crawling up behind them, gaped as well.
“Bweeegh!”
“...So that was it.”
It must have been rough. After a fast, heavy burst of vomiting, Hyuk looked half-dead as he spoke.
“I think this is as far as I go.”
Anyone looking at him might have taken him for a wounded soldier who’d been stabbed while fighting bravely.
I gripped his shoulder hard.
“Mujin. You can do this.”
“No. I’m finished. I’ll only be a burden if I go.”
“A burden? You’re an excellent meat shie—”
“Excuse me?”
“Shield! You’re the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s shield!”
“I could have sworn you said meat shield.”
Ignoring Hyuk’s suspicious muttering, I hauled him to his feet. Right now, even a meat shield—no, a single extra hand—was precious.
Besides, apart from me, Hyuk was the strongest meat shield in the reconnaissance squad. Damn, it kept slipping out.
I deliberately lowered my voice.
“Our family is in danger, and you’re saying you want to run?”
If it had been me, I would have run.
“No, sir!”

A twenty-first-century office worker would have spat in your face and walked away even if you promised to file it as a workplace injury, but the reconnaissance squad was more loyal than I’d expected. Hyuk drew his sword, his face pale.
“Very well. If a martial artist has to die, he should die fighting.”
“That’s a fine resolve, but don’t die.”
“You just called me a meat shield.”
“You don’t trust me?”
“Yes.”
Hyuk’s answer was as sharp as a blade, and quiet laughter spread through the reconnaissance squad. The tension in my body, frozen by my first large-scale battle, eased a little.
I grinned and tightened my grip on my spear.
“Eyes wide, ears open. Follow my orders, and you’ll make it back alive.”
That was a vow I was making to myself. I would get these guys out alive somehow.
Please don’t die.
I didn’t know how this war would end, or who would live and who would die.
All I could do was give it everything I had.
“Let’s go.”
At that, we charged forward like a gale. We were an arrow with me at the tip, and our target had already been chosen.
The Head Elder.
Clear in the distance, I could see a white-haired old man. At his feet lay a fallen man surrounded by a pool of blood.
A ball of fire surged up from my gut.
“That’s my brother...”
I pulled a spear from where it had been driven into someone’s corpse like a gravestone. Then, in the next instant—
“Get your hands off him, you bastard!”
The spear shot straight ahead, devouring the hundreds of feet between us.
Someone in the reconnaissance squad let out a muffled cry.
“We got him!”
That was when the Head Elder’s sword moved.
Shuk.
A streak of light. The spear split in half and bounced away to either side.
Same result as before. But this time, we’d closed the distance considerably, so I saw it clearly.
The blue flash that surged along his blade for an instant.
Aura?
No. Why was that showing up here?
Aura.
A crystallization of mana that only an A-rank Hunter or higher could draw out.
Mana and internal energy were different only in name. Both were forms of qi. And since this was Murim, that made it Sword Energy.
Sword Energy.
Heh heh heh.
Fuck. Are you kidding me?

I’d known for a long time that the Head Elder was a master. I’d even been prepared to fight him if it came to that. The problem was that a Head Elder who could use Sword Energy hadn’t been part of the plan.
This is a bit much.
I glanced aside and saw more than ten pairs of trembling eyes.
Hyuk Mujin’s were practically undergoing an earthquake.
“C-Captain.”
“Y-Yeah?”
“That just now... looked like Sword Energy.”
“Yeah...”
“Can you use Sword Energy too?”
“If I could, I would’ve used it already. Even Jopil wasn’t at that level.”
“Right?”
“Right. But aren’t you exhausted?”
“I feel like I’m going to throw up.”
As if we’d agreed on it, we slowed down. We’d gone from the hundred-meter dash to race walking, but it still felt like we were walking into a lion’s jaws.
“Uh, Captain.”
Hyuk spoke with every trace of color drained from his face. Judging by his complexion alone, he could have passed for a white man.
“Are you sure the Head Elder betrayed us?”
“I’m sure.”
“Could it possibly be a misunderstanding—”
Before he could finish, three or four black-clad men charged at us with a shout.
“Protect our lord!”
“For the Head Elder!”
Get a load of those lines. They’d work perfectly as a toast at a Jin Family of Taiyuan year-end party.
I cut down every last black-clad man charging us, then looked at Hyuk.
“Uh, what were you about to say?”
“...Nothing.”
Having failed to win the argument in his own head, Hyuk hung his head with a grim expression.
But only for a moment. Step by step, the closer we drew to the Head Elder, the more desperately he searched for a way out.
“Why do people have to fight?”
Is this bastard aiming for the Nobel Peace Prize?
“You said earlier you’d fight and die. Like a martial artist.”
“That was the worst-case scenario. Wouldn’t it be better to settle this with a conversation?”
“Talking would be nice. But they sent assassins after us first.”
“Oh.”
“And I threw a spear.”
“Ah.”
“And I cursed while throwing it.”
“Ah—ahhh.”
By the time we were within about a hundred feet of the Head Elder, Hyuk’s face looked like death. The other reconnaissance squad members didn’t say anything, but I could see them trembling.
Of course, I wasn’t much different. Just thinking about Sword Energy made my heart pound.
I’m well and truly screwed.
But I had no intention of running. If I had, I never would have come back in the first place. I would have been content with reality and simply kept living there.
I’d already come too far. There was only one path left.
“Stop.”
Everyone halted as if they’d been waiting for it. Hyuk’s face said he was hoping for a dramatic peace treaty, but I gripped my spear and stepped forward.
“W-Where are you going?”
“To fight. You wait here.”
“Are you insane? We’d be better off waiting for the Lesser Family Head and attacking together—”
“See the person lying over there?”
“Y-Yes.”
“That’s my brother.”
Hyuk stared at me as though the sky had fallen, then let out a deep sigh.
“Then I’m coming with you.”
“What?”
“Even a meat shield like me should bump our odds up by a hair, shouldn’t it?”
This guy actually came up with some admirable thoughts.
I snorted a laugh and turned away.
“You trying to get yourself killed? I’m just going to feel him out and come back. Wait here.”
The Head Elder was now barely thirty feet away.
A distance either of us could cross in an instant.
A heavy silence pressed down on the space between us. In those few moments, my palms grew damp.
Phew.
But I wasn’t an easy mark either. At Level 30, when I was only Second Rate, I’d already defeated Jopil, a Peak master. And I’d continued to improve after returning to reality.
Now that I was Level 40, I could proudly call myself a master capable of holding his own in either reality or Murim.
No. I was a master.
If I keep as much distance between us as possible...
In a fight where a few centimeters could decide life or death, a spear’s reach was a massive advantage.
I watched the Head Elder’s face and steadied my breathing.
This is doable.
I drew up my internal energy in a single burst and charged. Ten feet—the range where my spearhead could reach the Head Elder, while his sword couldn’t reach me.
Now!
I brought the spearhead down toward the crown of his head.
At the same time, the System notification I’d been waiting for rang out.
Ding.
System The effect of the Title Gambler is applied. Strength temporarily increases. Agility temporarily increases. Stamina temporarily...
The effect of the Gambler Title, which raised combat-related stats by ten percent in a one-on-one duel, seeped into every part of my body.
And on top of that—
Whoosh!
The increase in my stats accelerated the attack as well. The spearhead came down like a bolt of light, aimed at the crown of the Head Elder’s head.
This is going in.
I was certain.
Even a monster like Jopil wouldn’t have been able to dodge it. But the man I was facing wasn’t Jopil.
He was the Head Elder.
Boom!
The spear shaft shuddered with a thunderous crash. The Head Elder had blocked the spear with a movement too fast for me to see, and now he smiled faintly.
“Not bad. Better than I expected.”
Without even time to answer, I wrung out every last ounce of strength. The spear, loaded with tremendous force that even a decent master would have struggled to endure, crushed down on his sword.
Grrrkk.
With an ugly grinding sound, his sword slowly began to rise...
No. Wait.
It should be going down. Why is it coming up?
I’d put that much force into it, yet I was the one being pushed back. At my dumbfounded expression, the Head Elder’s smile deepened.
“You tried, but did you think that would be enough?”
The next instant, every hair on my body stood on end.
Tsssss.
A blue haze bloomed along the blade.
Sword Energy.
Before I could even react, the spearhead that had been slowly getting pushed back was sliced off like tofu.
Shing.
Now it wasn’t a spear but a staff. A long staff.
Sword Energy flashed again toward me as I backed away.
Shing.
The long staff became a short staff.
Shing.
Fuck. Even nunchucks would be longer than this.
I hurled the iron rod—no longer a spear or even a staff—at the Head Elder.
Shing.
“Do you intend to run?”
Run? What a hurtful thing to say.
I’d already thrown myself sideways the instant I released the rod. I grabbed the collar of the man lying facedown as though dead.
Got him!
My only goal from the start had been to rescue Jin Wikyung.
Now that I’d accomplished it, there was no reason to fight that monstrous old man. I clutched Jin Wikyung to me and launched myself away with all my strength.
Whoosh—boom!
The Sword Energy that came a beat later split the ground.
Hyuk Mujin and the reconnaissance squad surrounded us as we escaped the Head Elder’s range by a hair.
“Protect the Captain!”
“Are you all right?”
I said nothing. I forgot that we had to flee from the Head Elder immediately. I even forgot that we were standing in the middle of a battlefield.
My mind was consumed by a single question.
Who is this man?
I’d definitely rescued Jin Wikyung. I was supposed to have rescued him...
So who was this macho-looking middle-aged man in my arms?
His face was covered in blade scars, and his eyes were bloodshot. In a trembling voice, I asked,
“Excuse me, but who are you...?”
At that moment, Hyuk Mujin let out a startled cry.
“Gah! Lee Cheonbaek!”
Lee Cheonbaek? The name rang a bell.
“You know him?”
“Of course I do!”
“Are you close?”
“What kind of bullshit is that? That’s Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek!”
“Blood Wolf Sword?”
“Yes! That Blood Wolf Sword...!”
“Cool alias. Sounds like a master.”
Hyuk tore at his hair and shouted,
“He’s the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect! Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek!”
I scrambled backward.
This man was Lee Cheonbaek?
Cold sweat ran down my back.
He’s Lee Seogeun’s father.
He was the man who’d started a war because he thought I’d poisoned his son. He was also a cold-blooded killer who’d slaughtered adults and children alike in revenge.
As if rescuing the wrong man wasn’t bad enough, I nearly got stabbed for it.
But Lee Cheonbaek no longer seemed to have the strength left for that.
His whole body was covered in blood, and he couldn’t so much as twitch a hand. It looked like he’d suffered a serious Internal Injury or been subjected to a Pressure-Point Strike.
Still, at least it isn’t Jin Wikyung.
As if he’d read my mind, Hyuk asked,
“Then where is the Lesser Family Head?”
“I don’t know. And...”
I hurriedly yanked him back by the nape of his neck. A sword flew in and buried itself where Hyuk’s foot had been a moment earlier.
I’m really well and truly screwed.
I let out a deep sigh, then continued.
“You think that old man is going to let us go?”
The Head Elder burst into a hearty laugh.
“Ha ha ha! Have you ever seen such an insolent brat!”
“If I behave politely, will you let us go?”
“Don’t you think you’ve come too far for that?”
Tsssss.
Sword Energy surged up.
No more words were needed.
I pulled a spear stuck among the corpses. Then, with everyone’s eyes on me, I spoke.
“Encircling formation. Spread out.”
One of the oldest Hunter sayings went like this:
There are strong monsters, but no monster that can’t be taken down.
What made that possible was a raid.

“...Nothing.”
Having failed to win the argument in his own head, Hyuk hung his head with a grim expression.
But only for a moment.
Step by step, the closer we drew to the Head Elder, the more desperately he searched for a way out.
“Why do people have to fight?”
Is this bastard aiming for the Nobel Peace Prize?
“You said earlier you’d fight and die.
Like a martial artist.”
“That was the worst-case scenario.
Wouldn’t it be better to settle this with a conversation?”
“Talking would be nice.
But they sent assassins after us first.”
“Oh.”
“And I threw a spear.”
“Ah.”
“And I cursed while throwing it.”
“Ah—ahhh.”
By the time we were within about a hundred feet of the Head Elder, Hyuk’s face looked like death.
The other reconnaissance squad members didn’t say anything, but I could see them trembling.
Of course, I wasn’t much different.
Just thinking about Sword Energy made my heart pound.
I’m well and truly screwed.
But I had no intention of running.
If I had, I never would have come back in the first place.
I would have been content with reality and simply kept living there.
I’d already come too far.
There was only one path left.
“Stop.”
Everyone halted as if they’d been waiting for it.
Hyuk’s face said he was hoping for a dramatic peace treaty, but I gripped my spear and stepped forward.
“W-Where are you going?”
“To fight.
You wait here.”
“Are you insane?
We’d be better off waiting for the Lesser Family Head and attacking together—”
“See the person lying over there?”
“Y-Yes.”
“That’s my brother.”
Hyuk stared at me as though the sky had fallen, then let out a deep sigh.
“Then I’m coming with you.”
“What?”
“Even a meat shield like me should bump our odds up by a hair, shouldn’t it?”
This guy actually came up with some admirable thoughts.
I snorted a laugh and turned away.
“You trying to get yourself killed?
I’m just going to feel him out and come back.
Wait here.”
The Head Elder was now barely thirty feet away.
A distance either of us could cross in an instant.
A heavy silence pressed down on the space between us.
In those few moments, my palms grew damp.
Phew.
But I wasn’t an easy mark either.
At Level 30, when I was only Second Rate, I’d already defeated Jopil, a Peak master.
And I’d continued to improve after returning to reality.
Now that I was Level 40, I could proudly call myself a master capable of holding his own in either reality or Murim.
No.
I was a master.
If I keep as much distance between us as possible...
In a fight where a few centimeters could decide life or death, a spear’s reach was a massive advantage.
I watched the Head Elder’s face and steadied my breathing.
This is doable.
I drew up my internal energy in a single burst and charged.
Ten feet—the range where my spearhead could reach the Head Elder, while his sword couldn’t reach me.
Now!
I brought the spearhead down toward the crown of his head.
At the same time, the System notification I’d been waiting for rang out.
Ding.
System The effect of the Title Gambler is applied.
Strength temporarily increases.
Agility temporarily increases.
Stamina temporarily...
The effect of the Gambler Title, which raised combat-related stats by ten percent in a one-on-one duel, seeped into every part of my body.
And on top of that—
Whoosh!
The increase in my stats accelerated the attack as well.
The spearhead came down like a bolt of light, aimed at the crown of the Head Elder’s head.
This is going in.
I was certain.
Even a monster like Jopil wouldn’t have been able to dodge it.
But the man I was facing wasn’t Jopil.
He was the Head Elder.
Boom!
The spear shaft shuddered with a thunderous crash.
The Head Elder had blocked the spear with a movement too fast for me to see, and now he smiled faintly.
“Not bad.
Better than I expected.”
Without even time to answer, I wrung out every last ounce of strength.
The spear, loaded with tremendous force that even a decent master would have struggled to endure, crushed down on his sword.
Grrrkk.
With an ugly grinding sound, his sword slowly began to rise...
No.
Wait.
It should be going down.
Why is it coming up?
I’d put that much force into it, yet I was the one being pushed back.
At my dumbfounded expression, the Head Elder’s smile deepened.
“You tried, but did you think that would be enough?”
The next instant, every hair on my body stood on end.
Tsssss.
A blue haze bloomed along the blade.
Sword Energy.
Before I could even react, the spearhead that had been slowly getting pushed back was sliced off like tofu.
Shing.
Now it wasn’t a spear but a staff.
A long staff.
Sword Energy flashed again toward me as I backed away.
Shing.
The long staff became a short staff.
Shing.
Fuck.
Even nunchucks would be longer than this.
I hurled the iron rod—no longer a spear or even a staff—at the Head Elder.
Shing.
“Do you intend to run?”
Run?
What a hurtful thing to say.
I’d already thrown myself sideways the instant I released the rod.
I grabbed the collar of the man lying facedown as though dead.
Got him!
My only goal from the start had been to rescue Jin Wikyung.
Now that I’d accomplished it, there was no reason to fight that monstrous old man.
I clutched Jin Wikyung to me and launched myself away with all my strength.
Whoosh—boom!
The Sword Energy that came a beat later split the ground.
Hyuk Mujin and the reconnaissance squad surrounded us as we escaped the Head Elder’s range by a hair.
“Protect the Captain!”
“Are you all right?”
I said nothing.
I forgot that we had to flee from the Head Elder immediately.
I even forgot that we were standing in the middle of a battlefield.
My mind was consumed by a single question.
Who is this man?
I’d definitely rescued Jin Wikyung.
I was supposed to have rescued him...
So who was this macho-looking middle-aged man in my arms?
His face was covered in blade scars, and his eyes were bloodshot.
In a trembling voice, I asked,
“Excuse me, but who are you...?”
At that moment, Hyuk Mujin let out a startled cry.
“Gah!
Lee Cheonbaek!”
Lee Cheonbaek?
The name rang a bell.
“You know him?”
“Of course I do!”
“Are you close?”
“What kind of bullshit is that?
That’s Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek!”
“Blood Wolf Sword?”
“Yes!
That Blood Wolf Sword...!”
“Cool alias.
Sounds like a master.”
Hyuk tore at his hair and shouted,
“He’s the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect!
Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek!”
I scrambled backward.
This man was Lee Cheonbaek?
Cold sweat ran down my back.
He’s Lee Seogeun’s father.
He was the man who’d started a war because he thought I’d poisoned his son.
He was also a cold-blooded killer who’d slaughtered adults and children alike in revenge.
As if rescuing the wrong man wasn’t bad enough, I nearly got stabbed for it.
But Lee Cheonbaek no longer seemed to have the strength left for that.
His whole body was covered in blood, and he couldn’t so much as twitch a hand.
It looked like he’d suffered a serious Internal Injury or been subjected to a Pressure-Point Strike.
Still, at least it isn’t Jin Wikyung.
As if he’d read my mind, Hyuk asked,
“Then where is the Lesser Family Head?”
“I don’t know.
And...”
I hurriedly yanked him back by the nape of his neck.
A sword flew in and buried itself where Hyuk’s foot had been a moment earlier.
I’m really well and truly screwed.
I let out a deep sigh, then continued.
“You think that old man is going to let us go?”
The Head Elder burst into a hearty laugh.
“Ha ha ha!
Have you ever seen such an insolent brat!”
“If I behave politely, will you let us go?”
“Don’t you think you’ve come too far for that?”
Tsssss.
Sword Energy surged up.
No more words were needed.
I pulled a spear stuck among the corpses.
Then, with everyone’s eyes on me, I spoke.
“Encircling formation.
Spread out.”
One of the oldest Hunter sayings went like this:
There are strong monsters, but no monster that can’t be taken down.
What made that possible was a raid.

chapters.title: Chapter 59
paragraphs: Shh-shh-shhk!
Jin Wikyung and Wipeng’s battle against the three Elders raged like a storm.
Sword strikes crashed together from every direction, too fast and fierce for an ordinary martial artist to follow.
Krshhk.
Blocked.
The instant Wipeng realized it, he twisted aside. The Second Elder’s sword grazed his hair as it thrust past.
The Second and Third Elders pressed him as though they were one.
“You bastards!”
Jin Wikyung charged with a roar, only for the First Elder to cut him off.
“Where are you rushing off to?”
Sword Energy shot upward, then plunged toward the crown of Jin Wikyung’s head.
The blow threatened to split him in two. Jin Wikyung hurriedly raised his sword to block. Pale Sword Energy wreathed his blade as well.
Boom!
A figure staggered back through the cloud of dust kicked up by the thunderous impact. Jin Wikyung’s face had gone pale. He spat out bloody phlegm.
What the hell kind of internal energy...

He had trained in exceptional martial arts and taken elixirs since he was a child, but this was a bad matchup. The First Elder was a vile old monster who had lived for more than one jiazi while concealing his black heart.
Together with the Head Elder, he was a living witness who had fought his way through the Great Faction War.
“You goddamn old bastard.”
The First Elder replied with a hearty laugh.
“Lesser Family Head, mind your dignity.”
But the First Elder was not nearly as composed as he appeared.
His trembling blade and throbbing wrist were proof enough.
To think they were this strong.
Even in a street brawl, numbers mattered. How much more would they matter in a fight between masters? Yet Jin Wikyung and Wipeng were stronger than he had expected.
Or perhaps an old man’s pride had led him to overestimate himself.
How cruel. Truly cruel.
One jiazi. He had accumulated profound internal energy over those sixty years, but even that could not halt the aging of his body.
If only I were ten years younger.
After a bitter jab at himself, the First Elder stepped toward Jin Wikyung.
The swords of his sworn younger brothers, the Second and Third Elders, grew fiercer still.
Shh-shh-shhk!
“Urgh!”
Jin Wikyung and Wipeng were gradually driven back. Having only just fought the Peak masters of the Mount Heng Sword Sect made their situation even worse.
Their vision began to swim. Small wounds multiplied across their bodies. Their hands and feet no longer moved as they wished.
We can’t keep this up.
Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened.
Fwoooosh!
The First Elder’s Sword Energy had been bearing down without pause when it abruptly changed course. In the next instant, a lightning-fast strike split its target.
Shhk.
Fwaaah!
A man staggered in a spray of blood. The sword he had aimed at the First Elder’s side had shattered beyond recognition, and blood poured from his chest like a waterfall.
The First Elder saw his face and clicked his tongue.
“Discipline Hall Master, you foolish friend. Did you want to die that badly?”
“F-First Elder...”
The Discipline Hall Master’s voice sounded ready to give out at any moment. Yet he neither fell nor stopped speaking.
“You have... violated the family’s laws.”
“Heh heh. And?”
“As the Discipline Hall Master of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, I command you. The guilty shall abolish their own martial arts and enter the Repentance Cave...”
Shhk.
The First Elder answered with his sword.
The Discipline Hall Master had a nature as unyielding as bamboo, but his martial arts were not particularly advanced. He could neither see nor evade the stroke that pierced his throat.
Fire blazed in Jin Wikyung’s eyes.
“You bastard!”
Jin Wikyung was not the only one enraged. The Discipline Hall Master’s death set fire to the hearts of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s senior members.
“Discipline Hall Master!”
Before they were martial artists, they were human.
They had lived long enough to have much they had built, and much they had to protect. That was why they had feared it: a Peak master’s prowess, thrown away on a dog’s death.
But the Discipline Hall Master’s dignified end brought emotions they had briefly forgotten boiling back to the surface.
Shame and anger.
“Strike down those traitors!”
“Show them the spirit of the Jin Family of Taiyuan!”
Those most ashamed of themselves were the first to charge. They were the senior members who had belonged to the so-called Council of Elders faction.
They could not forgive themselves for helping the traitors. Nor could they forgive the Elders who had betrayed both them and the family.
“Fools.”
Shhk. Shhk. Shhk.
Every time the three Elders’ swords flashed, another life was extinguished.
The difference in strength was clear. Even so, the Elders’ wrinkled faces stiffened.
These bastards...!
Dozens of First Rate masters surged in from every direction without fear of death, each prepared to take an enemy with him.
It was not their martial arts that rattled the Elders, but their sheer momentum.
And amid that disruption, two men seized the opening without hesitation.
Shhk.
“Gah!”
A scream tore from the Third Elder’s mouth. Before he knew what had happened, Wipeng’s Sword Energy had surged up and carved through his side.
“Little brother!”
The Second Elder wavered at the scream of the sworn brother who had stood beside him for decades. For the briefest instant, his attention shifted elsewhere.
It cost him dearly.
Three swords thrust out at once, grazing him from head to toe. As the Second Elder hurriedly retreated, a bolt of lightning shot toward him.
Fwoooosh!
The instant he felt something cold burrow into his back, the Second Elder knew it was over.
Thuk!
It split flesh and severed bone. The Sword Energy rampaged like a living thing, tearing through his blood vessels and searing them.
How long had it been since he had felt pain like this?
The Second Elder’s vision went white. Soon, he could no longer feel any pain at all.
“I, Jin Wikyung, Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, have cut down the Second Elder!”
As Jin Wikyung ripped his sword from the Second Elder’s chest and roared, the Third Elder’s head was falling not far away. Wipeng, soaked in blood, lifted it high.
“Here is the Third Elder’s head!”
The survivors took up the cry.
“Wipe out the traitors!”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan is not the enemy of the Mount Heng Sword Sect! Lower your swords!”
The shouts ringing out across the battlefield rallied the Jin Family’s martial artists.
With its leadership all but wiped out, the Mount Heng Sword Sect had yet to find its bearings. Before long, however, its martial artists turned their weapons on the black-clad men.
“What are you doing? Those Jin Family bastards are right in front of us—”
“Enough of your nonsense. The only ones attacking us are those bastards in black!”
He was right. The Jin Family’s martial artists were following their command’s orders to the letter, and Mount Heng’s people realized one of their enemies had dropped away.
The black-clad men who had appeared out of nowhere were now their common enemy.
“Show them the strength of the Mount Heng Sword Sect!”
“I don’t know where you crawled out from, but wipe them all out!”
Once the two forces joined together, it was the black-clad men who began to give ground.

They were elites hardened by brutal training, but the deaths of the two Elders inevitably shook their morale. Blades rushed in from every direction, giving them no chance to recover, and the black-clad men began to fall one after another.
“Aaargh!”
“Don’t fall back! Anyone who retreats will die!”
Even in that chaos, the First Elder swung his sword without a word.
Everything within his sight, everything within his reach, was his enemy.
Shhk.

Twenty? Thirty? He no longer knew. Like a man possessed, the First Elder cut down everything that stood in his way. Among them were people who had once addressed him with reverence and young men who looked barely twenty.
What does age matter when it comes to life and death? Anyone who stands before a blade is a person of Murim.
At last, a bear of a man blocked the path of the First Elder, who was drenched in the blood of dozens. His eyes looked ready to burn everything to ash.
“Why did you do it?”
“Wealth and glory. To seize the Jin Family of Taiyuan and swallow all of Shanxi.”
The answer came without a hint of hesitation. Everyone trembled with rage.
Everyone but one.
Jin Wikyung shook his head.
“That isn’t the answer I wanted.”
“Then answer it yourself, Lesser Family Head. Why would my brothers, my lord, and I do such a thing?”
“Revenge.”
Jin Wikyung continued in a quiet voice.
“The grand plan you spoke of wasn’t meant to win you wealth and glory or make you ruler of a single province. Too many opportunities for that have already passed, and you’re all old. And...”
“Enough.”
“The Head Elder has no descendants. Neither do the Second Elder, the Third Elder, or you.”
At that moment, a livid spark flared in the First Elder’s placid eyes.
It was the anger he had suppressed for many long years, a remnant that surfaced for the briefest moment before sinking again.
“Why did you do it?”
Instead of answering, the First Elder raised his sword and pointed it at Jin Wikyung.
No—the tip pointed over Jin Wikyung’s shoulder, toward someone somewhere beyond him.
“Hear it from him yourself.”
In the end, the Head Elder held the final key.
Jin Wikyung strode toward the First Elder.
“I will. After I cut you down.”
“Can you really afford to take your time like this?”
“What do you—”
Jin Wikyung’s frown froze.
Taekyung!
His youngest brother, the apple of his eye, was holding off the Head Elder.
The instant he remembered what he had momentarily forgotten, all the blood in his body seemed to turn cold.
If I delay any longer, something irreversible will happen.
The moment Jin Wikyung grasped the full situation, his voice rang out like bitter frost.
“Wipeng. Take the First Elder.”
“I obey.”
“The rest of you, lend him your strength.”
“We follow the Lesser Family Head’s command.”
Wipeng and some ten surviving senior members spread into a wide ring around the First Elder.
“Everyone else, follow me and open a path! We’re going after the Head Elder!”

Jin Wikyung was about to depart with several dozen guards when he glanced back at the First Elder. Though his end was approaching, the old man showed no sign of agitation. If anything, he looked relieved.
“First Elder.”
“Do you have something left to say?”
Jin Wikyung tossed out a single sentence.
“By the authority of the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, I expel you from the family.”
“Heh heh. Heh heh heh!”
Leaving the First Elder’s laughter behind, Jin Wikyung raced toward the battlefield.
Dozens of black-clad men tried to stop him, but the tide had long since turned. Martial artists surged in from every direction and hacked them apart.
“Open a path!”
“It’s the Lesser Family Head! Kill anyone who stands in his way!”
It was only a moment. For Jin Wikyung, an eternity passed.
Taekyung. Please, please...
He could not even bring himself to think the word death.
How long had he run with his pounding chest clutched in his arms? When he finally reached his destination, his eyes flew wide.
What is this...?
The scene before him was utterly shocking.
Raid.
Until a few decades ago, it was a word used only in games.
But after the Demon King appeared and the Great Cataclysm began, raids became the defining symbol of Hunters.
Countless real battles had been fought and countless lives sacrificed along the way. Building on that experience, Hunters had finally established the modern method of raiding.
Tank, damage dealer, healer.
The tank blocks. The damage dealer attacks. The healer heals.
It sounded simple, but becoming a licensed Hunter required studying a mountain of raid manuals and proving yourself through actual combat.
Hunter training camp... That was a living hell.
But because I endured it, I came out a Hunter. Now, as a seven-year veteran, I can pull the right position and the right response for any situation.
And right now—
“Hey, throw dirt! Keep throwing it!”
I realized that everything I’d learned wasn’t worth shit.
Tank? Healer?
Fuck...
I was a fucking moron for thinking ten melee damage dealers counted as a raid.

Jin Wikyung strode toward the First Elder.
“I will.
After I cut you down.”
“Can you really afford to take your time like this?”
“What do you—”
Jin Wikyung’s frown froze.
Taekyung!
His youngest brother, the apple of his eye, was holding off the Head Elder.
The instant he remembered what he had momentarily forgotten, all the blood in his body seemed to turn cold.
If I delay any longer, something irreversible will happen.
The moment Jin Wikyung grasped the full situation, his voice rang out like bitter frost.
“Wipeng.
Take the First Elder.”
“I obey.”
“The rest of you, lend him your strength.”
“We follow the Lesser Family Head’s command.”
Wipeng and some ten surviving senior members spread into a wide ring around the First Elder.
“Everyone else, follow me and open a path!
We’re going after the Head Elder!”
Jin Wikyung was about to depart with several dozen guards when he glanced back at the First Elder.
Though his end was approaching, the old man showed no sign of agitation.
If anything, he looked relieved.
“First Elder.”
“Do you have something left to say?”
Jin Wikyung tossed out a single sentence.
“By the authority of the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, I expel you from the family.”
“Heh heh.
Heh heh heh!”
Leaving the First Elder’s laughter behind, Jin Wikyung raced toward the battlefield.
Dozens of black-clad men tried to stop him, but the tide had long since turned.
Martial artists surged in from every direction and hacked them apart.
“Open a path!”
“It’s the Lesser Family Head!
Kill anyone who stands in his way!”
It was only a moment.
For Jin Wikyung, an eternity passed.
Taekyung.
Please, please...
He could not even bring himself to think the word death.
How long had he run with his pounding chest clutched in his arms?
When he finally reached his destination, his eyes flew wide.
What is this...?
The scene before him was utterly shocking.
Raid.
Until a few decades ago, it was a word used only in games.
But after the Demon King appeared and the Great Cataclysm began, raids became the defining symbol of Hunters.
Countless real battles had been fought and countless lives sacrificed along the way.
Building on that experience, Hunters had finally established the modern method of raiding.
Tank, damage dealer, healer.
The tank blocks.
The damage dealer attacks.
The healer heals.
It sounded simple, but becoming a licensed Hunter required studying a mountain of raid manuals and proving yourself through actual combat.
Hunter training camp...
That was a living hell.
But because I endured it, I came out a Hunter.
Now, as a seven-year veteran, I can pull the right position and the right response for any situation.
And right now—
“Hey, throw dirt!
Keep throwing it!”
I realized that everything I’d learned wasn’t worth shit.
Tank?
Healer?
Fuck...
I was a fucking moron for thinking ten melee damage dealers counted as a raid.

chapters.title: Chapter 60
paragraphs: The Head Elder thought,
Have I lived too long?
The Murim he remembered had not been like this. Martial artists had not been like this.
Ganging up on an opponent was shameful. Ambushes were condemned. A man who got so much as dirt on his back became a laughingstock.
And yet...
“Throw dirt! Keep throwing it!”
In all his eighty years, he had never seen anything like this. What? Throw dirt?
It was a cheap, cowardly trick that not even the Demonic Cultists he had fought like mortal enemies decades ago had stooped to using.
Is that bastard truly a martial artist?
Even more appalling was the reaction of his so-called subordinates.
“Squad Leader’s orders! Throw dirt!”
“Keep your distance! Watch the Sword Energy!”
Watching the men obey without a word made his head spin.
What kind of goddamn bastards are these?
They were not martial artists.
No, they were not even human.
This was an insult to all martial artists—and to the Head Elder himself, who had devoted his entire life to the sword.
“How dare you...”
He was drawing his sword when—
“You idiots!”
A stern shout rang out half a beat sooner. A young man whose face was swollen as though he had been stung by a swarm of bees swept a fierce glare around him.
“What the hell do you think you’re doing?”
He looked ridiculous, but he had real spirit. Yes. That was how a martial artist ought to behave.
At least one of them has some sense.
The Head Elder was nodding to himself when the young man shouted,
“You think dirt’s enough? Mix in rocks too!”
The Head Elder shuddered as though struck by lightning.
The humiliation was so unprecedented that he forgot even to swing his sword as a clod of dirt flew straight into his face.
Splat!
He could say with certainty that in all his eighty years, he had never taken an attack so humiliatingly or with his guard so completely down.
As the dirt pattered off him, he spotted a hefty rock thoughtfully mixed in with it.
“Uh-heh. Uh-heh-heh-heh.”
The Head Elder laughed like a madman.
Then his laughter abruptly stopped.
At the same moment—
Tssssss.
Sword Energy surged from his blade, laden with one jiazi of internal energy.
“Are you prepared?”
Jin Taekyung watched him and muttered,
“Shouldn’t have mixed in the rocks...”
Before the words had even left his mouth, the Head Elder charged like a lion. The dozen or so sheep screamed and scattered.
“Spread out! Spread out!”
“Keep throwing dirt!”
Even as they fled, they did not forget to throw dirt.
Fwoooosh—
A fierce gale blasted from the tip of the Head Elder’s sword. Sand, dirt, stones—it made no difference. Before that overwhelming power, everything shattered and scattered.
How are we supposed to fight this guy?
Head-on?
Calling us melee damage dealers was being generous. If I sent the reconnaissance squad against the Head Elder, they’d be dying in heaps before I could blink.
I’d gotten attached to the bastards, though. I couldn’t let them die like dogs for nothing.
“Caaaptain!”
That bastard deserved to die, sure.
Why did you have to mix in rocks? Seriously, the rocks.
The Head Elder’s first target was Hyuk Mujin. Naturally. He had boldly struck the opening blow.
I heaved a deep sigh and launched myself toward him.
Shiiiiing!
I thrust my spear at the Head Elder’s chest with all my strength.
The Sword Energy about to carve through Hyuk Mujin’s back immediately changed direction.
Shing.
That goddamn Sword Energy.
There was no time to look at the spearhead it had sliced clean off. I snatched the terrified Hyuk Mujin by the scruff of his neck.
“Run!”
But the Head Elder was not about to give up so easily.
Swoooosh!
The air shrieked, and my side burned. A mere graze tore away a handful of flesh and sent blood spraying.
Kh.
It hurt like hell. But right now, even screaming was a luxury.
I need to buy time.
I shoved Hyuk Mujin aside and turned back. The Head Elder raised an eyebrow.
“You?”
It was only one word, but the meaning came through perfectly.
You think the likes of you can stop me?
I answered as calmly as I could.
“Yeah. Me.”
“Do you not value your life?”
“If I tell you it’s damn precious, will you let me live?”
“Heh heh. What an insolent tongue for one so young.”
“Gramps, does your pecker still stand?”
Tssssss.
It rose ramrod straight.
Large, magnificent Sword Energy.
“...Still going strong, I see.”
The hand gripping my spear grew slick with sweat.
Looks like I’ll have to use every last trick I’ve got if I want to survive this.
I had far more secrets than the Head Elder knew.
I could attack using my Inventory, and I had One Annihilation—a Skill that poured several times my normal strength into a single blow.
I’ve never shown it to anyone, just in case something like this happened.
Was this what people in Murim called a final, last-resort technique?
One thing was certain. Neither the Head Elder nor anyone else in Murim would see it coming.
And on top of that...
“Encircling formation. Form up.”
Shff.
Hyuk Mujin and the reconnaissance squad began closing in from every direction.
A flimsy net for a fish as big as the Head Elder.
But with a sharp enough harpoon, we had a chance.
“You think this will be enough?”
“To catch one old man? More than enough.”
The Head Elder smiled, amused.
“What a fearless brat. The kind who only comes to his senses after a beating.”
But he never got the chance. A voice suddenly cut in.
“I must have misheard you. Say that again.”
A mountain of a man stood there, his eyes wide and fierce. The voice that emerged from between his thick lips was cold as ice.
“You said you were going to lay a hand on our boy?”
Fwoooosh.
Sword Energy blazed up along his blade like wildfire and pointed at the Head Elder.
Jin Wikyung had appeared like a savior. He winked at me.
“Well? Your big brother looks cool, doesn’t he?”
Still the same.
It was the first time I had seen that face in a month.
The moment Jin Wikyung appeared, the tension drained from my body.
I was glad.
Just glad.
Thank goodness he’s alive.
Wikyung was covered in blood, as though he had fought a brutal battle to get here. Wounds large and small showed through the tears in his clothes.
But that was enough. All that mattered was that he was alive.
There’s a lot I want to say, but it can wait.
We could have our reunion after the war was over. Wikyung seemed to feel the same way. He turned his gaze forward.
At the end of our gazes, the Head Elder slowly began to speak.
“If you have made it this far, then...”
Jin Wikyung’s icy voice cut him off.
“The Second and Third Elders are dead. The First Elder is only a matter of time.”
That was good news. If Wikyung put it that way, the Elders must have played a major role in this war.
The Head Elder had lost his hands and feet.
“Did the two of them... go peacefully?”
“Probably.”
The Head Elder nodded readily.
“They always said they wished to die fighting as martial artists. They got their wish. I’m glad.”
“They’ll be remembered as traitors, not martial artists. Every last one of you.”
“History is written by the victors.”
The Head Elder leveled his sword at us. Even before dozens of men, including me and Jin Wikyung, he stood utterly composed.
“Now, let us decide who the victor will be.”
Jin Wikyung opened his mouth as if he had something to say, then closed it firmly.
The next moment, a thunderous roar burst from him.
“Strike down the rebels!”
Shing. Shrrring.
Dozens of weapons were drawn at once, all aimed at a single man. It was quite a sight.
“We obey!”
With a tremendous shout, dozens of martial artists charged as one. I was no exception. My grip tightened around my spear, and my chest felt ready to burst.
We can win. No. We win, no matter what.
It was an all-out melee without the slightest formation. But we had Jin Wikyung, a Peak master, and dozens of martial artists at his back.
And there’s me.

The Head Elder had placed too much faith in his own strength. He had committed every last man to the front without keeping even a minimal guard around himself. As a result, the black-clad men were now pinned down by the combined assault of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect.
The Head Elder...
dies right here.
It’s over!
It did not take long for that certainty to shatter.
Shushushushush!
Dozens of tiny points shot out of nowhere, slicing through the air faster and harder than any of us had expected.
“It’s the finger-flicking technique!”
Jin Wikyung’s shout rang out, but I had no time to wonder what that was.
Pow-pow-pow-pow!
Clang!
“Aaargh!”
“Guh!”
Some men fell. Others knocked the projectiles aside.
Those who fell did not rise again.
Don’t tell me...
It had lasted only an instant, but I had seen it clearly. Tiny fragments were embedded like buckshot around their hearts and across their faces.
Stones?
They were little more than shards now, but they had definitely been stones. Unable to withstand the Head Elder’s internal energy, they had shattered the moment he fired them at us.
That’s possible?
Goose bumps rose across my skin, but it was not over.
The Head Elder was extending one hand toward us.
“Scatter!”
This time, Wikyung and I shouted at once. The martial artists, already on high alert, scattered in every direction.
Good. We weren’t too late this ti—
My relief lasted only a moment.
Swoooosh!
This time, what came shooting at us was not the finger-flicking technique.
It was the Head Elder.
He plunged into the martial artists and rampaged among them like a wild beast.
Slash. Slash. Slash.
“Grrk.”
“Hhk.”
Each time his sword flashed through the darkness, another life went out. Wherever the Head Elder passed, he left only strangled screams and corpses behind.
“Head Elder!”
Jin Wikyung charged at him in fury. By then, the Head Elder had already killed five people. Yet his pale face remained untouched by so much as a drop of blood, making him look like a ghost.
“You’ve come?”
“How dare you!”
“You’re all so clumsy. Peace must have lasted too long.”
There was one undeniable fact.
The Head Elder was a hero of the Great Faction War.
He was stronger and more experienced than anyone else here—a Peak martial artist honed through countless battles.
Shiiiiing!
The Sword Energy Jin Wikyung unleashed stabbed through empty air. The Head Elder evaded it with nothing more than a slight tilt of his head, then flicked a finger.
His target was me.
Shhk!
I could not see a thing, but instinct told me what it was.
Internal energy.
It was exactly that—a solid mass of qi.
I threw myself into a roll without hesitation.
Pshk.
“Guh.”
I should have blocked it with my spear, but the attack was too unfamiliar for me to think that far ahead.
An unnamed ally paid the price with his life.
I felt rotten.
“Narye tagon? You truly are a donkey.”
I spat out the dirt in my mouth.
“When your life’s on the line, you do whatever it takes.”
“Haha. You’ve already become a proper man of Murim.”
Clang! Clang-clang-clang!
What kind of monster was this?
Even as he spoke, the Head Elder deflected every one of Jin Wikyung’s Sword Energy attacks. The sight left me speechless.
Thud!
Even then, a fist loaded with internal energy smashed the skull of a martial artist who’d gone for his back.
“You’re still twenty years too early.”
The battle had barely begun. Not even enough time had passed to drink a cup of tea, yet nearly twenty martial artists had already become cold corpses.
“You bastard!”
Shiiiiing!
A middle-aged warrior whose face looked vaguely familiar lost his head to Sword Energy.
“Die!”
Boom!
A young man with a baby face that might have been twenty had his chest caved in and dropped to his knees.
They were not NPCs.
They were real people.
Faces I had seen at least once around the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Faces belonging to people whose hands I had shaken.
I gritted my teeth.
I’m sorry.
I was not apologizing because I lacked the power to stop it. I was apologizing because I had used their deaths.
Shhk!
Another man fell to the Head Elder’s finger-flicking technique like a puppet with its strings cut. But just as the corpse seemed about to topple backward, it sprang upright like a roly-poly toy.
Then it pitched toward the Head Elder.
“Cheap trick!”
Boom! Bang!
With one hand, the Head Elder blocked Jin Wikyung’s sword. With the other, he sent a palm strike hurtling into the corpse.
And then...
Now.
Hidden behind the corpse as it flew through the air, I thrust my spear.
“One Annihilation.”
The next instant—
Goooooong.
A deafening roar left my ears numb.

He had felt his life threatened this keenly only a handful of times. Every hair on his body stood on end, and the world slowed.
Shiiiiing!
Jin Taekyung’s spear came from the front, while Jin Wikyung’s sword flew in from behind. The two brothers’ coordinated attack came together with perfect timing.
A true life-or-death moment.
Fwoooosh.

The one jiazi of internal energy coiled in the Head Elder’s dantian spread through every limb and bone. It poured vitality into his aging muscles and woke his blood vessels. The change did not stop there.
Tssssss.
The Sword Energy that had extended nearly a foot compressed to half its length.
But this was not a loss of power. It was a concentration of it.
The threadlike Sword Energy wrapped around the entire blade, taking the shape of another sword.
Sword Force.
The symbol of the superhuman masters who had broken through the wall of the Peak realm and opened a great new domain.
It was still incomplete, no more than half-formed, but it was unmistakably Sword Force—the culmination of the martial arts the Head Elder had spent his life mastering.
Shhk.

Even the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s ancestral treasure sword was severed, Sword Energy and all. Jin Wikyung’s internal energy scattered in an instant, the shock wrenching his insides. His face went pale.
One stroke would have been enough to take his neck.
But the Head Elder had no time.
Shwack!
He reached for the spear now almost at his chest. His wrinkled hand, too, was wrapped in a dazzling radiance of qi.
It, too, was an incomplete Palm Force, but it was enough to stop Jin Taekyung’s spear.
No. It looked like enough.
Kraaaaaash!
Until the vortex pouring from the spearhead swallowed him whole.
A deathly silence descended. It felt as though the dozens gathered here—perhaps everyone on the battlefield—were watching us.
No.
Not us.
One man.
“This...”
At the center of countless gazes, the Head Elder slowly opened his mouth.
“What form was that?”
I answered.
“One Annihilation.”
Even saying the words brought on a ravenous hunger. Every muscle in my body stung, and not a scrap of internal energy remained inside me.
But that was all.
Unlike when I’d fought Jopil, I neither passed out nor collapsed pathetically to the ground.
My body can handle it now.
I had grown strong enough to withstand One Annihilation’s side effects. And as I had grown, so had One Annihilation’s power.
The Head Elder’s condition was proof of that.
“One Annihilation. One Annihilation...”
Muttering under his breath, he pressed an acupoint on his shoulder.
The bleeding stopped, but that was all. The arm ground away without a trace by One Annihilation’s vortex did not return.
“I never thought I’d end up one-armed at my age. Heh heh.”
The Head Elder gave a hollow laugh and turned toward Jin Wikyung.
“You have a frightening younger brother.”
Jin Wikyung asked, his face wan, “Does that child frighten you?”
“What about you?”
“I’m proud of him.”
There was not a hint of hesitation in his answer. A smile spread across his pale face.
“I raised him like gold and jade, but he grew into steel. That’s the kind of child Taekyung is.”
The Head Elder stared at his smile.
“You’re quite a capable man. Worthy of shouldering the future of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Am I?”
“But not as much as your younger brothers.”
Jin Mukyung had reached the Peak realm at twenty, so that was understandable. But ranking even me that highly was almost more praise than I could handle...
What is he getting at?
As though he had read my mind, the Head Elder continued.
“Power is the one thing a man will not share, even with his own blood. When the time comes, will you still be so proud of your younger brothers?”
The air around us went ice-cold in an instant.
Everyone facing the Head Elder at close range belonged to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Cautious looks clung to my cheeks, then quietly slid away.
Family Head? I have no intention of becoming anything like that, you bastards.
That was when Jin Wikyung spoke.
“So that was it.”
Bitterness and relief mingled in his voice. The Head Elder’s brow twitched.
“What are you talking about?”
“The reason you betrayed us. The reason today came to pass.”
The Head Elder’s trembling eyes answered for him. I sighed inwardly.
So that was what this was about.
A succession struggle.
It felt as though a huge piece of the puzzle had clicked into place. The smaller pieces still out of position began falling into place one by one as they spoke.
“What happened?”
Jin Wikyung asked respectfully.
The shift in his tone was so natural that no one else seemed to notice.
“Do you know anything about your grandfather?”
“I have heard nothing. Father never spoke a word of him.”
“He was a coldhearted man. Toward his children and his only younger brother alike. And...”
The Head Elder gave a dry little laugh.
“He was petty. For many reasons, we gradually drifted apart despite once being close brothers. Then it happened.”
“The Great Faction War.”

“Have you heard of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples? They came in endless waves. The Murim Alliance was formed, but it was little more than a coalition of the Nine Sects and One Gang, each too busy defending its own territory.”
That was also when the Head Elder had begun making a real name for himself.
He rallied Shanxi’s martial artists beneath the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s banner and ultimately drove out the Demonic Cult’s forces.
“The final battle took place right here, at Eight Spring Gorge.”
His gaze seemed to grope toward some distant point in the past.

“It had been a long war. Many had died, and everyone was exhausted. But we still had hope—the hope that we could finally return to our families. All three hundred members of the death squad shared that hope.”
“In the end, you won a great victory.”
Three hundred against three thousand.
The result was the Demonic Cult’s annihilation.
It was a glorious victory and the reason the Head Elder was still remembered to this day. Everyone had believed that without question.
Until just now.
“There was an ambush.”
What?
“We fought while retreating deep into the gorge, but we were hopelessly outnumbered. Even as I swung my sword like a madman, one question refused to leave me.”
The Head Elder’s voice was chillingly calm.
“How could they have set an ambush in advance? My elder brother should have been blocking the road into Eight Spring Gorge.”
Silent shock rippled through the crowd. The last traces of color vanished from Jin Wikyung’s already pale face.

“The battle lasted half a day. We fought waiting for reinforcements that never came, and it was useless. Of the three hundred volunteers, only eight survived. When we finally returned to the family, I have never been able to forget the look on my brother’s face when he saw me.”
“Is that... true?”
“Enough time has passed for mountains and rivers to change several times over. Did you think I had come this far on mere suspicion?”
Decades were more than enough time for suspicion to harden into certainty. The Head Elder laughed hollowly.
“My brother turned the war into an opportunity. I became a hero on the battlefield, but he became Family Head. Everyone who had followed me either died in battle or vanished afterward.”
“Then was that why you entered the Council of Elders immediately afterward?”
“Because only then would he feel at ease. Because only then could my people and I remain alive.”
My people?
I thought back to what he had said. The eight survivors who had followed the Head Elder and lived to the end.
It wasn’t difficult to guess who they were.
The Elders and the Sect Leaders of the Five Gates of Shanxi.
The survivors had sworn revenge—revenge against the Family Head and the family that had betrayed them.
The Head Elder slowly swept his gaze over the crowd.
“It had been a very long wait.”
Silence swallowed everyone. Disbelief, shock, shame—their emotions differed, but no one could bring themselves to speak.
Well, no one except me.
“You sure dragged that bullshit out.”
I couldn’t hold back the little snorts of laughter leaking out of me.
I had listened all the way through to see where this was going, and this was what I got.
“In the end, you only have one goal.”
I jerked my thumb at the Head Elder.
“Revenge, my ass. You’re trying to become the man on top, aren’t you?”
“What did you say?”
“I’m right, aren’t I? Get rid of everything in your way—the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Mount Heng Sword Sect—and swallow Shanxi whole.”
“You insolent—!”
Had the old man swallowed a locomotive boiler? Oh, right. No trains here.
“Revenge? Sure. Fine, revenge...”
I picked at my ear and continued.
“But why now?”
This had happened a full forty years ago. Even counting the Head Elder’s age, he had waited half his life.

“How many of the people who stabbed you in the back are even still alive? There’s being late, and then there’s this. And please, I’m begging you—don’t give me that bullshit about a junzi waiting ten years to take revenge.”
If waiting ten years made you a junzi, did waiting forty make the Head Elder Jesus?
This was nothing more than a crazy old man trying to justify himself.
“You run your mouth just because you’ve got one.”
“I did. What are you going to do about it?”
“Do you think you know everything?”
“Do I need to? After things have gone this far?”
The question was so obvious I snorted a laugh and pointed at the battlefield.
A mountain of corpses and a sea of blood. Utter pandemonium. The scene before us was exactly that.
“That...”
The cold light in the Head Elder’s eyes wavered. But only for an instant.
“I see. What more is there to say?”
He muttered the words in self-mockery, then raised his sword.
“Head Elder.”
Jin Wikyung’s lips moved, but that was all.
This fight would end only when one side died. They had come too far to turn back.
“Come.”
I wasn’t about to refuse.
“Attack!”
It was time to hunt the wounded beast.
I remembered the day I first saw the Head Elder.
A bearing and dignity that made his age meaningless. His white beard called an immortal to mind.
Fwoosh!
Of course, there were no immortals who mercilessly cut people in half.
Even rotten, a prized fish is still a prized fish.
Drenched in blood, he swung his sword without pause. Everyone stared at him with a mixture of awe and fear.
“Monster...”
The Head Elder had lost an arm, but he was still strong.
He was clearly no longer as strong as before, though.
This is doable.

The Head Elder might have been a Peak master, but the martial artists here were the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s elite. They had fought across the battlefield under Jin Wikyung and were skilled enough to have survived their earlier clash with the Head Elder.
Clang-clang-clang!
The Head Elder knocked away the blades driving at him from every direction, his face darkening. Before, he would have used Sword Energy to cut through everything in his path.
It was proof that the internal energy that had once seemed like an inexhaustible spring was finally running dry.
On top of that, his aged body had reached its limit.
Shraaaak!
Sword wounds began to multiply across the Head Elder’s body. Unlike before, most of the blood was now his.
Now!
I wasn’t about to miss that opening. I drove my spear forward with all my strength, tearing a handful of flesh from his side.
“Hk!”
Even through the pain, the Head Elder cut down another martial artist and lunged at me. He had clearly set his mind on killing me; faint Sword Energy gathered along his swinging blade.
But...
Shhk.
The Sword Energy scattered in a rising spray of blood. Jin Wikyung appeared behind the staggering Head Elder.
“I’d forgotten you were there.”
The Head Elder turned, his face twisting.
“Did my elder brother teach you to put a blade in someone’s back?”
“My family members are dying. Is a sneak attack really that important?”
“Aren’t you ashamed as a martial artist?”
“I am the Lesser Family Head before I am a martial artist.”
“The Lesser Family Head, is it? Heh heh.”
Jin Wikyung regarded the Head Elder with a complicated expression.
“The tide has already turned.”
“So? Are you going to ask me to surrender?”
“Please put an end to this meaningless fight.”
The battle had turned in our favor long ago. But the black-clad men continued their stubborn resistance, and the screams and corpses showed no sign of diminishing.
“You’re right. Perhaps this is a meaningless fight. But...”
The staggering Head Elder straightened his back. A sharp gleam flashed in his eyes, and a blade-like aura began to rise from him.
“We’ve come too far to stop.”
A last desperate struggle?
No. It was more than that. Someone suddenly came to mind.
Jopil.
The Head Elder’s current appearance overlapped with Jopil’s final moments before his death.
Innate qi. He’s drawing out his innate qi.
Internal energy was acquired power accumulated by circulating qi and consuming elixirs. Innate qi was the opposite—the foundation of the human body, life force itself.
The Head Elder was staking his life to use it.
“Cough.”
He spat out blood and raised his sword. His life was fading rapidly, yet his sword shone more brilliantly than ever.
The moment I saw that overwhelming sight, a single word slipped out of me.
“Sword Force...”
It was instinct.
My heart pounded from the mere sight of it. I could feel a terrifying power that far surpassed Sword Energy.
And then—
“Yes. You were here.”
His blood-red eyes, their capillaries bursting one after another, locked on me.
Jin Wikyung lunged to stop the Head Elder.
“No!”
But the Head Elder had already vanished from where he stood.
In a single step he compressed fifty feet and brought his sword down on me.
Whoooong.
So this is how I die.
It was an attack I could neither dodge nor block.
I was dead. I was going to die.
But...
I can’t die like this.
I wrung every ounce of strength from my muscles. The last scant handful of internal energy raced toward the spearhead.
It was a final struggle, and a show of respect for the life I had lived so fiercely until now.
“One Annihilation.”
Shiiiiiiing!
My final strike, carrying every last bit of strength I had, shot forward.

My aching muscles, my heavy feet, my empty dantian—all of them swelled with new strength.
At the same time, I knew what I had to do.
One Annihilation.
Once more, a white vortex erupted.
Kraaaack!
A narrow escape.
Never in my life had those four syllables hit so close to home.
I had really died and come back. I’d even seen a vision of going through immigration into hell, sharing a passionate hug with Yama, and snapping a commemorative photo together.
If it hadn’t been for Lee Cheonbaek, that vision would have become reality.
Good thing I saved him.
I wanted to close Lee Cheonbaek’s eyes so he could rest in peace, but there was still work to do.
“Should’ve lived a decent life, then. Just a little.”
The Head Elder gave a quiet laugh. He looked horrific.
One Annihilation had swallowed his remaining arm, and it hadn’t stopped there—it had punched a hole the size of a fist through his chest.
“What a nasty-hearted brat. Have you no manners toward a dying old man?”
“The old folks I know spend their twilight years enjoying their grandchildren’s antics. They don’t run around trying to kill them like you, you old bastard.”
“Why, you brat! Try acting like a grandson before you say something like that.”
He laughed heartily. He looked deflated, yet relieved, as though he had finally let go of everything.
“Taekyung is a good kid. If you had opened your heart first, the two of you might have been close as grandfather and grandson.”
The Head Elder turned his head.
Jin Wikyung stood there, sword in hand.
“Are you planning to stab me with that sword?”
“I’m considering it.”
“You’d better finish considering it quickly. I don’t have much time left.”
His words were true.
Even now, as he talked as though nothing were wrong, blood poured like a waterfall from the severed stumps of both arms and from his lower abdomen.
On top of that, there was the backlash from drawing out his innate qi.
The fact that he was still alive felt like a miracle.
“You look like you’re suffering.”
“No. I’m growing comfortable.”
The answer was firm.
“I was barely thirty when the Great Faction War began. After that, I never once rested easy—not even for a moment. No...”
The Head Elder went on in a strained voice.
“In truth, perhaps I’ve been tired for a very long time.”
I muttered in disbelief.
“You did all that, and now you’re coming out with this?”
“Taekyung!”
Jin Wikyung sent me a mildly reproachful look, but the Head Elder did not seem offended. A breathy laugh escaped his closed lips.
“Puh-huh. Yes, you’re right. Just think of it as a senile old man’s bullshit.”
“Looks like it really is time for you to die.”
“Hey! You little brat!”
“What? It’s not like I said anything wrong.”
The Head Elder watched Jin Wikyung and me bicker through fading eyes.
“There was a time when we were like you two. Yes. There certainly was.”
But he no longer had time to linger over those memories.
“Cough! Guaaack!”
The Head Elder staggered after vomiting what looked like a whole bowlful of blood.
He was at death’s door. Every capillary in his eyes had burst, and the blood pouring from his body had long since pooled at his feet.
Anyone could see there was no hope left for him.
He’s really dying? That Head Elder?
Everyone dies.
Hundreds of lives had vanished on this battlefield alone—perhaps more than a thousand.
But the Head Elder’s death was something I had never even been able to imagine.
That was how overwhelming his martial prowess had been. It made his current state look all the more wretched.
And that only made me more curious.
“Why are you holding on this hard?”
The Head Elder answered.
“Because I want to tell those who went before me... that I did my best.”
“Any regrets?”
“None.”
He smiled broadly and thrust out his chest.
“Finish it. With your own hands.”
I raised my spear.
Jin Wikyung wore a troubled expression, but he did not try to stop me.
Shhk!
A single gust of wind passed, and the Head Elder’s knees—which had seemed incapable of ever buckling—touched the ground.
A peaceful smile appeared on his wrinkled face.
At the final moment, his lips moved, but no sound came out.
That was all.
